body:
## Blocked work

Blocks native NZBGet acceptance in #290 and draft #335. Keep Homarr Link preflight retryable Manual before creating or updating credentials; standalone NZBGet readiness and Link removal remain separate.

## Source-confirmed conditional logging risk

At both researched Homarr source `ebbd4876d25a51151444a009ab596e1154d62880` and recorded image OCI-source revision `3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348`, the NZBGet adapter embeds its username/password in the RPC path. A rejected request can retain that Address through the original `ResponseError` cause into downstream logs without credential-path redaction.

- [Adapter, lines 116–123](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/integrations/src/download-client/nzbget/nzbget-integration.ts#L116-L123): credential-bearing RPC path.
- [ResponseError, lines 5–10](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/common/src/errors/http/response-error.ts#L5-L10): retains response Address.
- [Integration settling, lines 39–44](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/api/src/settle-integrations.ts#L39-L44): logs rejected cause.
- [Error formatting, lines 22–53](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/core/src/infrastructure/logs/format/error.ts#L22-L53) and [metadata formatting, lines 9–14](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/core/src/infrastructure/logs/format/metadata.ts#L9-L14): recursively format causes and string properties without path redaction.

The [integration error decorator](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/integrations/src/base/errors/decorator.ts#L37-L145) sanitizes its own log copy, but rethrows the original cause; that does not protect downstream sinks. Ordinary connection-test 401/403 response payloads omit the Address and are not the established surface here.

The formatted text reaches the [Console transport](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/core/src/infrastructure/logs/transports/index.ts#L7). With Redis logging and log-view permission, it can also reach [Redis log history](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/core/src/infrastructure/logs/transports/redis-transport.ts#L28-L51), the [log API](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/api/src/router/log.ts#L55-L60), and the [browser log terminal](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/apps/nextjs/src/app/%5Blocale%5D/manage/tools/logs/terminal.tsx#L159-L165).

Every cited file was independently compared byte-for-byte at the two source revisions. This is source evidence, not attestation of built-image contents. No real credentials, rejected-credential runtime probe, log read or observed live leak was involved. Dedicated blocker searches found no duplicate; #332 and #350 cover different boundaries.

## Resolution and acceptance

- Establish a supported upstream transport using HTTP Basic headers, or complete credential-path redaction across every downstream error/log sink. Do not invent a configuration switch, disable authentication, add a proxy framework, or substitute direct App data for native Homarr data.
- Reconcile any changed Homarr version/image with the shared compatibility contract and review its exact source before activation.
- Only then authorize bounded native data, negative-auth/privacy and rendered/lifecycle verification with owned disposable credentials and redacted evidence. Source agreement and a currently valid login are insufficient acceptance.

This ticket is private tracker coordination, not public disclosure, runtime permission, native completion or approval to publish private source.
title: Homarr: block NZBGet activation until credential-path errors are safely redacted

body:
## Blocker

PatchMon 2.1.3 has no supported read-only credential for Homarr's GetHomepage statistics endpoint. This blocks #291 and keeps draft #345 on hold. A consumer sending only GET requests does not make its credential read-only: the same pair passes the server's host-enrollment authentication checks.

**Evidence classification: source inspection and previously recorded OCI registry metadata only. No runtime enrollment/exploit was attempted or demonstrated.** No credentials, private logs or host data are included. This ticket is private maintainer coordination, not a public upstream disclosure or authorization to contact/change an upstream provider.

Open and closed issue searches for PatchMon, GetHomepage and enrollment found no existing ticket covering this credential-authority boundary. Closed #81, #97 and #103 concern startup/password/session defects, not this blocker.

## Exact versions and source evidence

The identities below were observed over HTTPS on 11 October 2026 for linux/arm64; tags are mutable, and registry metadata is not runtime compatibility proof.

| Image                                    | Index digest                                                              | Platform manifest digest                                                  | Config digest                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ghcr.io/patchmon/patchmon-server:2.1.3` | `sha256:9eba4008c8e25f72929752bba7499b5deda26cf5de3e4678dbf760d16822b2f2` | `sha256:54d587af0871a8d6369386c8d2e8830d20f03b69f51b19cf5c6cb5bf5356a2ed` | `sha256:e22cecbb743cdabffd50fbc6a06293c7ad29eacd41d0d08556c954305860904c` |
| `ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:v2.4.1`      | `sha256:ee67a5e856c051c4e114418a54b89a3fc3cb5507d0689e5cb89c790305c549cd` | `sha256:308feba8b9845cbdb21eb2e1b05579d49fb815bf3f0a452e58b59fcd4db8ecd2` | `sha256:c6d895d659718b05ab9cc7b936458e6f5820b5cf3f0d35318588bd1b6901ee1b` |

PatchMon's image revision label and `v2.1.3` tag resolve to Go source `354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c`; its version label is `2.1.3`. Homarr's actual image revision label is `3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348`, version label `main`; the v2.4.1 tagged baseline is `ebbd4876d25a51151444a009ab596e1154d62880`. Relevant PatchMon integration/widget/Stats contracts were byte-identical between those Homarr revisions; authenticated runtime `info.getInfo` was not verified in this lane.

- [Homarr adapter, exact actual image source](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/3d4150e59f600876b7e308f857b2f21572b75348/packages/integrations/src/patchmon/patchmon-integration.ts#L13-L58): both `patchmonApiKey` and `patchmonApiSecret` become Basic auth for `/api/v1/gethomepage/stats`.
- [PatchMon routes](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/server/router.go#L389-L411): GetHomepage requires `integration_type: gethomepage`; general API tokens with `host: get` scopes use a different API and cannot substitute. [Token issuance/listing](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/server/router.go#L719-L724) requires `can_manage_settings`.
- [Statistics authentication](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/middleware/api_auth.go#L75-L134): validates activity, expiry, matching integration type, bcrypt secret and optional IP ranges.
- [Enrollment handler](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/handler/auto_enrollment.go#L371-L429): validates the same active pair, expiry, IP ranges and daily limit, but never checks integration type/scopes before the [host creation path](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/handler/auto_enrollment.go#L432-L545). This is the source-backed reason enrollment authority cannot be described as read-only.
- [Issuance limit behavior](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/handler/auto_enrollment.go#L110-L138): `max_hosts_per_day` defaults to 100 and accepts only 1–1000, so requesting zero becomes 100. One-per-day still grants enrollment authority; it is not a read-only restriction.
- [Once-returned secret](https://github.com/PatchMon/PatchMon/blob/354ec8cdeb53338e57a8332fb2ddd5c7f307c75c/server-source-code/internal/handler/auto_enrollment.go#L196-L218): official issuance returns the pair once; token inventory does not recover a lost plaintext secret.
- [Private implementation evidence and remaining gaps](https://github.com/ajnart/selfhost-skills/blob/05f68f3bd937bdec2bb0efd32c0e171c08a794c2/docs/homarr-patchmon-contract.md).

## Required fix and acceptance

- [ ] Establish a reviewed upstream-supported image/version/digest/source contract that separates statistics-read authority from host enrollment and every other write/agent operation. A GET-only caller, IP restriction or daily limit is not an acceptable substitute. Do not assume an unverified newer version fixes this.
- [ ] Identify and document the actual minimum credential permissions accepted by the supported Homarr statistics adapter. The pair must authenticate statistics reads while being denied enrollment/credential-management/other write authority. Do not weaken authentication, fabricate keys, or silently switch to administrator JWTs/general API credentials.
- [ ] Use official headless issuance and verification with the Project administrator only for provisioning. Persist both credential halves and their returned ownership identity through existing helpers/Project secret boundaries; no database injection, secret files outside that boundary, arguments, output, screenshots or telemetry containing credential values.
- [ ] Reuse a valid recorded owned pair across Setup/reruns/restart, checking issuer ownership, activity/type/scope and authenticated statistics. No manual-resource adoption, broad rotation or deletion. Missing/rejected halves or a lost once-returned secret retain an actionable Manual recovery path rather than rotating unrelated keys or claiming success.
- [ ] Keep upstream coordination, image/version changes and runtime acceptance separately approved. Maintainer review decides any upstream contact; this issue itself authorizes none. Until a supported read-only contract exists, retain the Manual hold even when a manually created broader pair is available.
- [ ] No agent installation, host enrollment, host inspection, device privilege or package upgrades are part of credential readiness. Any disposable enrollment/inventory target needs its own explicit approval. Empty authenticated inventory is not proof of secure/fully patched computers; absent/incomplete inventory is not zero updates.
- [ ] After the source/credential boundary is resolved, record bounded approved negative-auth/authority and native data evidence with exact identities. Do not close #291 merely because this blocker is resolved: registry activation, real/rendered widgets, ownership and lifecycle acceptance remain separate requirements of #291/#262.

## Current boundary

#345 remains a draft with a fresh GET-only preflight and Manual credential hold; its descriptor is not registered. No supported read-only pair was issued or adopted, and no native/rendered/lifecycle completion is claimed. This follow-up changes tracker metadata only; source, worktree, draft status, runtime, dependencies and tests remain untouched.
title: PatchMon: establish statistics-only credentials without enrollment authority

body:
## Blocked native Link

Blocks #279 and draft #327. Source inspection of Homarr 2.4.1 (`ebbd4876d25a51151444a009ab596e1154d62880`) and the Catalog's Gluetun 3.41.3 shows that native VPN and Stats summaries cannot currently use the existing least-privilege control credential safely.

`GluetunIntegration.getSummaryAsync` always requests VPN status, DNS status, public IP and `GET /v1/vpn/settings`. Gluetun's settings handler JSON-encodes a full copied VPN configuration; its OpenVPN and WireGuard types expose credential/private-key fields. Homarr's settings schema also requires those fields, although the displayed summary only uses protocol/provider. This is an unnecessary provider-secret read boundary, not evidence that secrets were rendered or leaked.

The current Project control role grants only `GET /v1/vpn/status`, `GET /v1/publicip/ip` and `GET /v1/portforward`. It correctly denies DNS/settings reads. Broadening it to the credential-bearing settings route is not an approved fix. Homarr also requires eight public-IP string fields, while Gluetun can omit empty metadata or clear it when disconnected.

The staged descriptor deliberately blocks before any native summary call. No runtime, provider connection, real credentials or functional acceptance was used to establish this finding.

## Acceptance

- Provide a first-party credential-free summary route or an audited supported Homarr adapter/version that uses only necessary non-secret data. Preserve the supported-version and exact credential-shape gates from #262.
- Native `status`/`publicIp` Stats must not require provider credentials or fabricated metadata. Treat stopped/unready tunnels, missing optional metadata, authentication errors and malformed responses distinctly.
- Preserve the current control grants, firewall and Compose authority. Do not add a credential-scrubbing proxy, disable TLS/authentication, purchase a provider account or discover a user's provider secrets without a separately approved design.
- Before registering `gluetunTarget()`, record exact versions/digests and prove useful authenticated native/rendered data plus rerun, credential recovery and removal preserving unrelated resources in an approved disposable Project.
- Keep #279/#327 blocked until that proof exists; a navigation tile, successful connection test or fake fixture is not acceptance.

## Sources

- [Pinned Homarr adapter](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/ebbd4876d25a51151444a009ab596e1154d62880/packages/integrations/src/gluetun/gluetun-integration.ts)
- [Pinned Homarr schema](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/blob/ebbd4876d25a51151444a009ab596e1154d62880/packages/integrations/src/gluetun/gluetun-types.ts)
- [Gluetun settings handler](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/blob/v3.41.3/internal/server/vpn.go)
- [Copied settings state](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/blob/v3.41.3/internal/vpn/state/vpn.go)
- [OpenVPN JSON fields](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/blob/v3.41.3/internal/configuration/settings/openvpn.go)
- [WireGuard JSON fields](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/blob/v3.41.3/internal/configuration/settings/wireguard.go)
- [Gluetun public-IP fields](https://github.com/qdm12/gluetun/blob/v3.41.3/internal/models/publicip.go)

Local source/gate notes: `docs/homarr-gluetun-contract.md` on draft #327 at `7d70c832c426eb1485ef8f072d461a621cfcabb1`.
title: Homarr/Gluetun: avoid provider-secret reads in native summaries

## What to build

Installing Umami (Catalog App ID: umami) and Homarr produces a verified native connection and useful Umami data, not just a navigation tile. Deliver one complete slice: the App's own Setup/readiness and credentials, the Homarr-owned Link, meaningful widgets, reconciliation/removal, and redacted functional acceptance. Reuse the compatibility and ownership contract established by #262; this peer may proceed independently of the other peer tickets after that reference slice.

## Upstream contract and App boundaries

- Upstream authentication alternatives: username and password, or API key; username/password is for self-hosted instances, while Umami Cloud requires an API key. Select a usable least-privilege mode without weakening existing authentication; alternatives are documented capabilities, not evidence that every mode works on every App version.
- Verify the self-hosted account/key and correct API base through Umami Setup; do not mistake the browser Address or default Cloud endpoint for the Catalog App's API.
- Native widget examples: Website Analytics/Umami and Stats widgets bound to a discovered or explicitly selected website.
- Use a disposable website and synthetic visits without collecting real visitors' personal data. Website identifiers and account/team permissions must be explicit; no Cloud account enrollment or public tracking deployment is implied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The App's own Setup establishes and verifies the account/API readiness above, creates or discovers any required credential through the existing Setup/helper and Project secret boundaries, and reuses valid credentials without unnecessary rotation. Existing Projects have a clear retry/recovery path. Unavoidable person/account/hardware steps stay explicit, retryable Manual steps; do not claim unattended success before they are satisfied.
- [ ] Homarr owns the Link and creates the correct native integration using the server-side internal Address separately from the browser Address. Verify the selected credential/API contract; rejected credentials, missing fields and unsupported capabilities yield actionable failure/wait states, never silent downgrade to unauthenticated mode or a tile-only success.
- [ ] Configure useful defaults from the native widgets above and supported Stats capabilities under #262's widget policy. Discover or explicitly select required identifiers and respect widget limits; never guess identifiers. Preserve other integrations' shared Stats/Calendar bindings.
- [ ] Demonstrate real API data through Homarr and at least one meaningful widget result using scoped owned data. Distinguish a valid empty dataset from authentication, unavailable hardware/upstream data and incomplete Setup. HTTP 200, container liveness, saved records and navigation alone are not acceptance; a mock-only or unavailable-hardware result cannot be reported as full functional proof.
- [ ] Reruns, restart and credential changes preserve stable owned integration/widget IDs and user-authored resources. Apply #262's explicit ownership/adoption policy: no silent adoption, update or deletion of manually created resources. Removal cleans up only this Link's owned resources/bindings and retains shared widgets still needed by others.
- [ ] An absent peer creates no integration attempt; an installed but unready peer retains an actionable wait. Verify both installation orders and late-peer installation/inbound Links, retry after readiness, and removal/reinstallation without duplicates or stale bindings. Keep existing JSON fields and persisted formats compatible; additions are additive.
- [ ] Prove the lifecycle only in a disposable isolated Project with approved scoped Compose resources and development Telemetry disabled. The person's Project, private files, credential stores and browser profiles are out of scope. No credentials in arguments, logs, screenshots or artifacts; no broad teardown, volume deletion, socket exposure, new host/device privilege or public Access. Additional account/hardware/network actions require explicit approval.
- [ ] Record exact tested Homarr and App versions, image digests where available, selected auth mode, redacted functional evidence, and unmet limitations. Reuse #262's supported version/capability checks and follow the repository's relevant local verification gate; a mutable tag is not compatibility proof. Do not claim untested auth alternatives or missing prerequisites passed.

## Sources

- [Official Umami integration guide](https://homarr.dev/docs/integrations/umami/).
- [Homarr v2.4.1 source/release baseline](https://github.com/homarr-labs/homarr/releases/tag/v2.4.1): authentication alternatives and native widget support were checked against this version. Revalidate against the exact version accepted by #262 before implementation.
title: Homarr: complete Umami Setup, credentials and verified widgets

Related to #194. The authorized static installer site can serve install.sh without changing repository visibility, but it does not make GitHub releases public.

Observed October 11, 2026 without authorization headers:
- https://api.github.com/repos/ajnart/selfhost-skills/releases returns 404.
- https://github.com/ajnart/selfhost-skills/releases/download/new-cli-v0.2.0/checksums.txt returns 404.
- The authenticated repository remains private; ajnart/selfhost does not resolve with gh.

The installer discovers release metadata and downloads checksummed archives from GitHub. Existing release binaries use the same GitHub API for self-update. Serving a public installer alone cannot complete either anonymously. Do not publish authenticated API responses or put a repository token into the site.

Acceptance:
- Maintainer approves an artifact-only public distribution channel without making the source repository public or changing that separate user-controlled decision.
- Distributable archives are built reproducibly from an identified commit and verified against approved SHA256 checksums before publication.
- Only approved CLI archives, checksums and minimal release metadata are public, never source archives, service configs or credentials.
- Installer release lookup and self-update use that channel, including an explicit compatibility path for existing binaries.
- Token-free scripts/verify-install.sh passes in its isolated HOME/install paths against the public installer, including a pinned old version upgrading.
- Keep the landing page explicit that public downloads are unavailable until the above passes.

No binary assets were published and no repository rename or visibility change was made.
title: Make anonymous CLI install and self-update possible while source stays private

## What

A reusable folder picker for path inputs in the Dashboard, so nobody types a full path blind. Start with the Media and Downloads folder fields in Onboarding.

## Behavior

- As the person types, the inputs list the directories inside the typed path. Typing `/media` shows what is in `/media`.
- Tab completes the common prefix or descends into the highlighted folder; arrow keys move through suggestions; Enter accepts the folder.
- Directories only, existing folders only. The current rule stays: the folder must exist or sit inside one that does.
- `~` expands to the home folder. Unreadable folders are skipped silently.
- Built as one reusable component (not Onboarding-specific) so other path fields can adopt it later.

## Constraints

- Prefer `huh`'s input suggestions (`SuggestionsFunc`) before writing anything custom. Only fall back to a `bubbles` filepicker modal if inline suggestions cannot do it.
- Filesystem listing goes through `internal/system/` so tests can fake it (`systemtest`).
- Keep the keybinds minimal and listed in the help.

## Done when

- Tests cover: listing, `~` expansion, nonexistent parent, permission errors, Tab behavior.
- Local gate from `CLAUDE.md` passes.

## What

Let a person scan an App's Address from their phone: a QR code modal in the Dashboard. Also bring back "This computer only" as a visible Access option, because the QR only makes sense once Access is explicit about who can connect.

## Behavior

- A keybind on the App detail view and an entry in the action menu opens a modal with the App name, its friendliest Address (the same one the Links show) and the QR code, rendered with Unicode half-blocks.

# Installation on hosts with existing services

**Purpose:** establish the intended product behaviour before proposing changes to installation and Access.

**From:** a project contributor, **To:** ajnart, project maintainer, **How your answers will be used:** define a proposal for review, not authorize implementation or changes to a host.

## Context

In my Homarr test on Patriot, installation succeeded but Homarr was only reachable through the server's loopback. Existing Access infrastructure was not integrated. Patriot's documentation describes Caddy with private Tailscale ingress, but we have not verified a live route to Homarr or established the cause of the test's binding. This is evidence of a user-facing gap, not a request to make Patriot's setup the standard architecture. The repository already supports a Dashboard and agent-facing commands. Its current Bring your own contract exports upstream details without changing an existing proxy. I need your intended direction before deciding whether to improve the CLI, add an agent workflow, or keep integration manual.

## How to answer

Allow roughly 10 minutes. No deadline is set. Short answers are enough. Partial answers and "I don't know" are useful. Please distinguish current requirements from possible future work.

## CLI and agent responsibilities

### Q1. What must someone be able to complete without an agent on a host with existing services?

For example, should the CLI cover App installation only, installation plus a supported Access option, or connection through an existing proxy?

> Answer: CLI already covers all of these, it doesn't support intelligently finding your Caddy file / reverse proxy and editing it for now, if it's simple we can create an issue for it (discovery or passing a absolute path to the config) I don't know so much about these atm. We must ensure the ROI on these is low. Does someone who already is knowledgeable enough about self hosting care about our cli / should care about it instead of doing all hand-made ? --> Don't think we need to support it that much (if it's hard/low ROI) 

### Q2. What role, if any, should an optional agent workflow have in understanding an existing host?

For example, an agent in Pi or Codex could inspect relevant host information, ask questions, and propose a plan while using self-host commands for Project changes.

> Answer: It can inspect the host to figure out info, depending on the level of the user as answered early in the skill, no need to explore on a fresh vps for example, it might also be low ROI to include too much stuff to "find" but it could be super beneficial to allow a step where the agent / cli can "migrate" existing containers (by accessing their container volumes) and using that as a starting point so that data isn't lost 

-> But it might be too hard to do the link/setup and ask the user for the actual username / password if we offer that    

### Q3. How should an unsupported existing Access setup be handled?

Possible approaches include an upstream export with manual instructions, an agent-assisted plan, or blocking until a supported option is chosen. No CLI can recognize every possible configuration.

> Answer: I don't get it 

## Existing infrastructure and permission

### Q4. May self-host itself configure an externally owned proxy or VPN after explicit approval?

_Why this matters: today Bring your own is export-only. Detecting infrastructure does not grant permission to change it._

> Answer: It's already done with CloudFlare + Tailscale support, other bring your own need to be setup by hand. In the future we can extend if we see trends about usage like people asking for a specific support   

### Q5. May an agent configure that external infrastructure after separate, scoped approval?

This is distinct from using self-host commands to change the Project.

> Answer: Yes, as a followup guideline. 

### Q6. What host information may be inspected automatically before approval?

Please define the boundary for discovery, such as listener metadata, service identities, networks, and explicitly supplied configuration. Credentials and private configuration require separate consideration.

> Answer: Everything? 

### Q7. What must always remain untouched during installation?

Consider existing services and their lifecycle, routes, networks, firewall rules, DNS, authentication, certificates, and data. Please identify any exceptions that require a separate operation.

> Answer: Everything mentioned above is already untouched as far as I know. If there is a port collide it would be nice to handle it gracefully, for example maybe two apps in the library share the same port, or something locally is already runner, we should offer the possibility to un-collide these by using the next available port 

## Completion and verification

### Q8. What must be true before telling the person that installation is complete?

_Why this matters: a working App on the server is different from an App the person can open through their chosen Access._

> Answer: Installation is complete when it works locally, no need to touch , low ROI 

### Q9. What evidence is required to claim that the chosen Address works?

A server-side HTTP response does not prove access from a phone, TV, or another computer. Should client-side confirmation be required, or should the CLI clearly report that it remains unverified?

> Answer: No confirmation. LOW ROI 

### Q10. How should a working App with unfinished Access be reported?

For example, should the result distinguish "App installed, Access pending" from a failed App installation?

> Answer: As suggested above ^ no need to handle it that much most likely 

## Anything else?

### Q11. What else should we know before proposing this behaviour?

TLDR is that Low ROI / Discoverability and "finding" the person's setup is not necessary / not wanted. Our tool is geared to beginners. Its role is to allow people to get into selfhosting for the first time. We provide a "batteries-included" setup for them to quickly get up on their feet. Advanced and opinionated users will be the loud minority if we start to support their advanced use-case it's a never ending battle. I think this tool must explicitly not have a high entry bar. 

In the future we could support cool stuff like authentik, authelia, global auth on the network, ... but that's for nerds and not needed for now. Not the goal of the tool in it's state, the mission statement is "Allow Linkedin Bros to post : Replace Netflix, Google Photos & Notion with this one Claude Code prompt! 🤯"  
These people will just ask Claude to "make it work on my phone"
title: Clarify installation and Access behaviour on hosts with existing services

## Summary

`self-host` 0.2.0 accepts Docker Compose v2.26.1 during host checks, but an App installation fails at the image-pull step because the CLI unconditionally requests Compose's JSON progress mode, which this Compose version does not support.

I encountered this during first-run onboarding after selecting only Homarr.

## Environment

- `self-host`: 0.2.0
- Docker Engine: 26.1.0
- Docker Compose: v2.26.1
- Host: Linux x86_64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use a host with Docker Compose v2.26.1.
2. Run `self-host` and complete first-run onboarding.
3. Select Homarr as the only App.
4. Approve the installation.

The underlying failure can also be reproduced without pulling or starting anything:

```console
$ cd ~/.self-host
$ docker compose --progress json config --services
unsupported --progress value "json"
```

On v2.26.1, `docker compose --help` lists only `auto`, `tty`, `plain`, and `quiet` as supported progress values.

## Actual behavior

The installation ends with:

```text
install homarr: exit status 1: unsupported --progress value "json"
```

Project state records the render step as successful and the pull step as failed. No Homarr container is created.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. `doctor` or onboarding rejects an incompatible Compose version before rendering the Project and gives a minimum-version upgrade hint, or
2. image pulling uses a compatible fallback when JSON progress is unavailable.

## Cause identified

`internal/compose/compose.go` runs every progress-aware pull as:

```text
docker compose --progress json pull ...
```

The host check in `internal/host/checks.go` only verifies that the Compose major version is at least 2. It therefore accepts v2.26.1 even though JSON progress was added in Compose v2.29.0.

Upstream comparison:

- [Compose v2.28.0 rejects values outside the older progress modes](https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/v2.28.0/cmd/compose/compose.go#L448-L457)
- [Compose v2.29.0 accepts `ui.ModeJSON`](https://github.com/docker/compose/blob/v2.29.0/cmd/compose/compose.go#L498-L506)

The system-test fixture currently reports Compose 2.29.7, so it does not cover an older Compose v2 host that passes `doctor` but cannot run pulls.

## Suggested coverage

- Test `doctor` or initialization with Compose v2.26/v2.28.
- Test that an incompatible version fails before App files are rendered, or test a non-JSON fallback path.
title: Install fails on Docker Compose <2.29: unsupported --progress value "json"

## What to build

Read `docs/agents/implementing.md` first.

Telemetry goes live with the maintainer's decisions:

- **Project key.** The public key is `phc_zY6Yg8ePwEfXC8FadEqkCcoCgzzy2u2VHjpaPTooBDfg` (EU PostHog, behind the `https://hog.ajnart.dev` proxy). It is a write-only public key, safe to embed. Make it the release default in `.goreleaser.yaml` (`envOrDefault "POSTHOG_PROJECT_KEY" "<key>"`). Development builds still send nothing.
- **Users counted once.** The install ID must stay stable, so one person on one machine counts as one user, even after deleting or reinstalling the Project.
  - Move it from the Home folder to the user config folder (`os.UserConfigDir()/self-host/telemetry-id`), migrating an existing `~/.self-host/telemetry-id`.
  - It stays random and is never derived from the machine.
  - Turn PostHog person profiles on (drop `$process_person_profile: false`) so unique users and retention count correctly. Set no person properties beyond what is already sent.
- **No IP.** GeoIP stays off and the payload never carries an IP. The maintainer enables "Discard client IP data" in the PostHog project.
- **Errors with stack traces.** Every `$exception` carries in-app stack frames (function, module-relative file, line; never absolute paths or user data) with a stable fingerprint. A panic anywhere in a command is captured as an unhandled `$exception`, flushed within the deadline, then the CLI exits as before. Each command event carries its steps with ID, outcome and duration, so slow and failing Setup steps show up. Check PostHog's current docs (via ctx7) for log ingestion. If a documented endpoint takes OTLP logs through the proxy, send warning and error log records with the same never-sent rules; otherwise say so in the PR.
- **No off-switch prompt.** There is no button or toggle to turn Telemetry off. The off switch stays the environment variables only (`SELF_HOST_NO_TELEMETRY=1`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, always off in CI and development builds).
  - The first-run notice says that anonymous usage data helps improve self-host, with no IP and no personal data, and links to the wiki page. It does not advertise the off switch.
  - The agent guide tells agents how to turn Telemetry off only when the person asks.
- **Docs in the GitHub wiki.** Telemetry documentation moves out of the README into a wiki page:
  - Add a `wiki/` folder in the repository holding `Telemetry.md` (what is sent, what is never sent, the install ID, the off switch) and `Home.md`, plus `scripts/publish-wiki.sh`, which copies `wiki/*.md` into `https://github.com/ajnart/selfhost-skills.wiki.git` and pushes.
  - The README keeps one line linking to the wiki page.
  - The wiki must be initialized once in the GitHub UI before the first push, so the script says so if the clone fails.
- **No dashboard yet.** Remove every public-dashboard placeholder. ADR 0006 says a public dashboard may come later.
- **ADR 0006 and `CONTEXT.md` (Telemetry)** are updated to match all of the above.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A release build carries the key, a dev build sends nothing (tests on the key and dev-build logic, plus `goreleaser release --snapshot` with the key set, checked with `go version -m` or a strings check).

body:
## Problem Statement

self-host works well for people who already know Docker, ports and reverse proxies. The people it is meant for do not. Picture someone who reads a LinkedIn post, has just started using AI with a Claude subscription and OpenClaw, and wants to stop paying for subscriptions and own their data. They have never used Docker, do not know what `192.168.0.5:8096` means, and cannot tell a good practice from a bad one, but their agent can run commands for them.

Today that person hits a wall at every step:

- **Finding the skill:** the skill is explicit-only, so a fresh chat ("where's the video thing again?") never loads it.
- **Learning the state:** a new conversation has no way to learn what is installed, where it lives or what each App is for.
- **Being taught plainly:** nothing asks whether they are new to this, so agents explain at the wrong level.
- **Reaching the Apps:** Apps are reachable only at `http://IP:port`. "I want to go to movies.mywebsite.com" has no answer, and the remote-access options are greyed-out "coming soon".
- **Recovering from errors:** when something breaks, the agent has no single place to read what went wrong.
- **Telling us:** neither the person nor the agent can say so, and we cannot see what people use.
- **Size:** the installed skill is about 790 files and 78,000 words of a legacy TypeScript CLI that the Go CLI has replaced.

## Solution

**For the person:**

- **Asked once:** the agent asks whether they are new or advanced and remembers the answer.
- **Plain words throughout:** every App, choice and step is explained in plain words, and the agent asks before every change.
- **First words matter:** the skill loads on its own, and a new conversation starts by asking the CLI what is installed and where.
- **Access:** one Access step offers friendly names at home, Tailscale for anywhere-but-private and Cloudflare Tunnel for their own web address, each with a diagram. The `IP:port` Address always keeps working.
- **A Recap at the end:** each App with its Address, where everything lives, and a few questions to explore next.

**For the agent:**

- `self-host debug <app>` reports what broke.
- `self-host feedback` reports a problem to us on purpose, after the person agrees.
- Anonymous Telemetry, published openly, shows what people actually use.

**For the repository:** it becomes `ajnart/selfhost`, with the Go CLI at the root and one small skill.

## User Stories

1. As a newcomer, I want my agent to ask once whether I am new to this, so that it explains things at my level.
2. As a newcomer, I want that answer remembered across conversations, so that I am never asked again.
3. As an advanced user, I want to say so once and get exact choices, flags and no hand-holding, so that I am not slowed down.
4. As anyone, I want to switch between New and Advanced at any time, so that the help fits as I learn.
5. As a newcomer, I want the agent to load the self-host skill on its own when I talk about running my own apps, so that I never have to know a slash command.
6. As anyone, I want the skill to cost almost nothing while idle (about 200 tokens), so that it does not crowd my agent's context.
7. As a newcomer in a fresh conversation, I want to ask "where's the movie thing again?" and get my App's Address, so that I never have to remember it.
8. As an agent, I want `self-host status --json` to say what each App is for, which Recipe it came from, which Address is the dashboard, and where the Home folder is, so that one command answers most questions.
9. As a newcomer reading `self-host status`, I want a short plain-English summary first, so that I understand it without reading JSON.
10. As a newcomer, I want everything self-host knows kept in one folder, `~/.self-host`, so that "where is my stuff?" has one answer.
11. As a newcomer without Docker, I want the agent to explain what Docker is in one sentence, ask whether to install it, and do it for me, so that I am never stuck at the first step.
12. As a newcomer, I want the agent to ask me one thing at a time through its question tool, so that I am never handed a wall of choices.
13. As a newcomer, I want a plain sentence before any change and a plain summary after it, so that I always know what happened.
14. As a newcomer, I want the agent never to ask me for a password or show one, but to point me at `self-host credentials`, so that my secrets stay out of chat.
15. As a newcomer, I want every App described by what it does for me ("Stream your movies to every screen"), not what it is, so that I can choose without research.
16. As a newcomer, I want one Access step that explains every way to reach my Apps with a diagram, so that I understand what each choice does.
17. As a newcomer, I want easy names at home such as `movies.local` or `movies.192-168-1-20.sslip.io` on first boot, so that I don't have to remember numbers.
18. As anyone, I want the `IP:port` Address to keep working whatever I choose, so that a broken name never locks me out.
19. As a person away from home, I want to reach my Apps privately from my phone with Tailscale, guided step by step, so that nothing is open to the internet.
20. As a person with a domain, I want `movies.mywebsite.com` through Cloudflare Tunnel with a login page in front, so that my family can reach it safely.
21. As anyone, I want an explicit yes that names the risk before anything becomes reachable from the internet, so that I never publish an App by accident.
22. As anyone, I want admin, database and downloader Apps kept private by default even with my own web address, so that the risky ones are never exposed.
23. As an advanced user, I want to bring my own proxy (SWAG, Pangolin, an existing Caddy or Traefik) and get each App's upstream from the CLI, so that self-host fits my setup.
24. As a newcomer, when setup finishes I want a Recap with each App, its Address, where my files are and how to sign in, so that I know what I have.
25. As a newcomer, I want a few opening questions at the end ("Want your own web address?", "Want to know what Jellyfin does?"), so that I can explore without knowing what to ask.
26. As an agent fixing a broken App, I want `self-host debug <app>` to print its Status, Addresses, failed steps, masked recent logs and what a working page shows, so that I can diagnose without guessing.
27. As an agent, I want agent-browser available to look at an App's page when the Debug report is not enough, after the person says yes to installing it, so that I can see what they see.
28. As a person who wants an App outside the Catalog, I want my agent to add it under `~/.self-host/extra/<name>/` and see it in the CLI and Homarr with its Address, so that everything lives in one place.
29. As a newcomer installing from the README, I want one copy-paste sentence for my AI, so that I never open a terminal myself.
30. As a person running the install one-liner, I want to be asked whether to add the skill to my AI agent too, so that I get both in one go.
31. As anyone, I want to be told plainly on first run that anonymous usage data is collected and how to turn it off, so that I can trust the tool.
32. As anyone, I want Telemetry off with one environment variable (`SELF_HOST_NO_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`), so that opting out is trivial.
33. As anyone, I want the collected data published on a public dashboard, so that I can see exactly what is sent.
34. As an agent, I want to send a Feedback report with `self-host feedback` after the person agrees, already redacted, with the CLI masking any known secret again, so that problems reach the maintainers.
35. As a maintainer, I want errors to arrive as PostHog exceptions with the version, OS and failed step, so that I can fix what breaks most.
36. As a maintainer, I want the repository to be `ajnart/selfhost` with the Go CLI at the root and the legacy tree gone, so that there is one product to maintain.
37. As an existing user, I want my installed CLI to keep updating after the rename, so that I don't have to reinstall.
38. As a script or agent, I want existing `--json` keys, non-TTY output and stored formats unchanged (only additive fields), so that my integrations keep working.

## Implementation Decisions

**Glossary and ADRs.** `new-cli/CONTEXT.md` gains Access, Address, Home folder, Profile, Experience level, Recap, Debug report, Telemetry and Feedback, and extends Unmanaged app. Exposure becomes a flagged legacy name. New ADRs:

- **0005:** agents load the skill on their own; approval, not activation, guards changes. It supersedes legacy ADR 0006.
- **0006:** Telemetry.
- **0007:** one repository, Go only.

**Repository.**

- The repo is renamed on GitHub to `ajnart/selfhost`, which redirects old URLs and keeps issues, PRs, releases and stars.
- In one commit, `new-cli/` moves to the root and the legacy tree is deleted: `.agents/`, `packages/`, the root legacy `scripts/` and `docs/` (keeping `docs/agents/`), and the packaging.
- The skill lives at `skills/self-host/SKILL.md`. `release.Repo` and `install.sh`'s `DEFAULT_REPO` change after the rename.

**Skill.**

- A short `SKILL.md` whose description says when to load it, at about 200 tokens. It routes to `self-host skill`.
- The guide gains:
  - the Experience level question, through the agent's ask-user tool;
  - the newcomer contract;
  - "run `self-host status --json` first in a new conversation";
  - Docker installation from Doctor's link;
  - agent-browser as an optional install offered with a yes/no;
  - the Recap with opening questions;
  - Debug report and Feedback usage;
  - Unmanaged apps under `extra/`.
- No goal-to-Recipe tables: agents work that out.

**Profile.**

- `~/.self-host/profile.json`, non-secret, created before any Project. A folder holding only the Profile, `appearance.json` or `extra/` is not a Project.
- New `self-host profile` (`--json`, `set experience new|advanced`).

**Status.**

- Additive fields: per App, `description` and `recipe` (recorded in Project state at install; additive) and `addresses` (friendliest first, `url` keeps the first). At the top level, `home` and `dashboard`.
- Plain `self-host status` starts with a plain-English summary.

**Catalog copy.** Every App and Recipe description is rewritten for newcomers: what it does for the person, under about 100 characters. A test keeps them present and bounded.

**Access.**

- One Onboarding step and one Settings section, each option with its diagram. Stored `EXPOSURE` values and `--exposure` stay; "Only this computer" leaves Onboarding.
- **Easy names at home:** the Project gets one managed Caddy owning the HTTP port. Each App gets `<app>.<ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io` and, where an mDNS announcer works (Linux first), `<app>.local`. The CLI checks which names resolve and lists only working Addresses.
- **From anywhere, privately (Tailscale):** guided auth key through the private-input path. The ticket decides between one Tailscale node per App, Tailscale Services, or one name with ports, after checking current Tailscale docs.
- **Your own web address (Cloudflare Tunnel):** a scoped API token. The CLI creates the tunnel, DNS records and a Cloudflare Access login policy before any route is live. Admin, database and downloader Apps stay private unless chosen one by one. Real HTTPS at home with the same domain (Caddy DNS-01) can follow.
- **Bring your own:** `self-host access export --format caddy|nginx|traefik` prints each App's upstream for SWAG, Pangolin or an existing proxy.
- **Shared rules:** one owner per port 80/443 and per DNS name; conflicts are reported, never overridden.

**Debug and Unmanaged apps.**

- `self-host debug <app>` (`--json`) assembles the Debug report from existing status, step, log and URL data, with secrets masked by the same redaction the event sinks use.
- Unmanaged apps are discovered under `~/.self-host/extra/<name>/compose.yml`, listed with Addresses, and covered by start, stop, update and backup.

**Telemetry and Feedback.**

- `posthog-go` (new dependency) sends through `https://hog.ajnart.dev` with a public project key: a random install ID in the Home folder (`telemetry-id`, never derived from the machine, so one install's events group together), anonymous events with no person profiles and GeoIP off, command events with duration and outcome, and errors as `$exception` with fingerprints.
- It sends in the background with a short deadline and never delays or fails a command.
- The first-run notice appears in Onboarding and in the first plain CLI command.
- `self-host feedback` takes the agent's text from stdin or `--message`, masks every known secret, shows it, asks yes/no on a terminal (`--yes` for agents after the person agreed in chat), and sends it as a `feedback` event.

**Install.** In the one-liner, `install.sh` asks over `/dev/tty`: "Add the self-host skill to your AI agent too? y/n". On yes it runs `bunx --bun skills@latest add ajnart/selfhost --skill self-host`, or `npx skills add` when only Node exists. Otherwise it prints the command and the copy-paste sentence. It never asks without a terminal.

## Testing Decisions

- **Seams:** the existing seams only.
  - The pure renderers and diagrams, with goldens.
  - The TUI Model harness, with goldens at 120×30 and 80×24, the 80-column check and the keybind audit.
  - CLI and service tests with fakes for Docker, Caddy, the Tailscale API, the Cloudflare API and PostHog.
  - App fragment, Setup and Link tests.
  - The guide coverage test, so every new command lands in the guide.
- **Telemetry:** a test captures every payload in a fake transport and asserts that the never-sent fields are absent, including paths, host names, inputs and known secrets. Another asserts nothing is sent with the off switches, in CI or in development builds.
- **Feedback:** tests that a known secret in the agent's text is masked before display and before sending.
- **Access:** tests that nothing becomes reachable from the internet without the separate explicit yes, and that admin and downloader Apps stay private by default.
- **No live runs:** no live Docker, Tailscale, Cloudflare or PostHog calls in tests.

## Out of Scope

- An MCP server.
- Migrating old `.selfhost/` projects from the TypeScript CLI.
- Ports and disk host checks (#140).
- Rootless Docker for the Beszel socket proxy (#187).
- Pangolin or SWAG as managed Catalog Apps; Bring your own covers them.
- Named volumes for App configuration.
- Native Windows.

## Further Notes

- CI cannot run (account billing), so every PR is gated locally as described in `docs/agents/implementing.md`.
- The showreel (PR #190) shows "Exposure" and the old install URL. It needs one text pass after the restructure and Access tickets land.
- At PostHog, the maintainer supplies the project key and the public dashboard, and turns on "Discard client IP data": no IP or location is kept.
title: Spec: self-host for everyone — newcomer path, Access, Profile, Telemetry, one repo

body:
## Problem

The Beszel socket proxy (#154) mounts `/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro`. The CLI supports rootless Docker (`internal/host/rootless.go`, Doctor's `docker-userns` check), where the daemon socket usually lives at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/docker.sock` and `/var/run/docker.sock` does not exist. On such a host the short bind syntax may create an empty directory at that path, and the proxy then reaches no Docker. The likely result is that Beszel shows this machine without per-container usage, and possibly a failing agent step. Not verified on a real rootless host.

## What to decide and build

- Verify on a rootless Docker host what happens today: the proxy start, the agent enrolment, and per-container stats.
- If it breaks, resolve the daemon socket path from the active Docker context (`docker context inspect` / `DOCKER_HOST`) when rendering the fragment. Keep the e2e isolation and appgen socket-mount exception exact: the target stays `/var/run/docker.sock` inside the proxy, and only the host source changes.
- Update `docs/catalog/traps/beszel.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Behaviour on rootless Docker recorded (runtime evidence).
- [ ] If needed: the proxy mounts the active daemon's socket on rootful and rootless hosts (fragment tests for both), and the socket-mount exception stays as narrow as today.
title: Beszel socket proxy on rootless Docker: socket path

## What to build

The maintainer picked **variant A, parallax starfield** for the pre-boot screen (#147/#148 shipped variant B). Replace B's scene with A in `internal/preboot`: three drifting star layers, aurora ribbons, shooting stars and sparkles, the ◆ pulsing with the purple → pink → cyan → gold sweep. On exit the stars stretch into streaks, then a slanted wipe brings in the Dashboard, the real one (the existing `RenderExit(..., under)` contract).

Drop the coffee theme: no cup, and no "Go grab a coffee". Instead a friendly time line: **"This should take about as long as <something>."** The comparison follows an estimate of the time remaining and changes as it goes, for example "a deep breath", "a song on the radio", "brewing a pot of tea", "a walk around the block". Before an estimate exists it shows a gentle warming-up line. The estimate comes from elapsed time and the pull fraction. It is smoothed with hysteresis, so the line does not flicker between buckets. Never a number of percent.

The donation keys stay (`c` Ko-fi, `s` GitHub Sponsors, `enter` skip) with neutral wording, for example "Like self-host? c Ko-fi · s GitHub Sponsors".

## Acceptance criteria

## Parent

#141

## What to build

Installing Beszel also monitors this machine. The Beszel App (`internal/apps/beszel/beszel.go`, hub `henrygd/beszel:0.20.0`) gains two services.

**Agent:** `henrygd/beszel-agent` at the hub's version, in WebSocket mode (v0.12+):

- `HUB_URL` points at the hub on `127.0.0.1`, with `TOKEN` and the hub's public `KEY`;
- `network_mode: host` and `LISTEN=127.0.0.1:45876`;
- `DOCKER_HOST` points at the proxy.

**Read-only socket proxy:** LinuxServer's socket-proxy, as Beszel documents, with container reads only (`CONTAINERS=1`) and writes denied. It is published on `127.0.0.1` whatever the Exposure, and it is the only service that mounts `/var/run/docker.sock`.

**Setup**, after `ready` and `admin-login`:

1. Read the hub's public key.
2. Get a permanent universal token with `GET /api/beszel/universal-token?enable=1&permanent=1`, signed in as the Admin login user.
3. Store the agent's settings in the Project's secrets.
4. Start the agent.
5. Check that this machine is listed as a system.

Every Check probes afresh, because `h.Step` re-runs Check after Do. `tools/appgen` and e2e isolation gain one named exception for this proxy only, recorded in `docs/catalog/traps/beszel.md`. Verify every image, environment variable and route against beszel.dev at implementation time.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fragment has the hub, the agent and the proxy, and only the proxy mounts the socket (fragment test).
- [ ] The agent listens on `127.0.0.1` and the proxy is published on `127.0.0.1` under both Exposures (test).
- [ ] The appgen rule still rejects every other socket mount, and the exception is named (test).
- [ ] Setup gets the key and token and checks the system against a fake hub, and its Checks probe afresh (tests).
- [ ] Secrets never reach the screen, logs or Activity text.

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately).
title: Beszel agent for this machine via a read-only socket proxy

The Backups sub-tab lists the archives in `<Project>/backups/selfhost-*.tar.zst`, with date, size and whether each is encrypted.

body:
## Problem Statement

After the TUI rework (#129), first feedback came from the maintainer and from a tester (Abdullah):

- In Onboarding, picking a Recipe doesn't show which Apps it will install.
- After approving the plan, the person waits minutes for images with nothing to look at, and with no invitation to support the project.
- The Where step's "local network" choice and the other Host settings are not understood.
- Nothing says that remote access is coming: a reverse proxy with HTTPS, Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel.
- App addresses on the Overview can't be opened with the terminal's own cmd+click.
- Installing Beszel installs only its hub. Nothing monitors this machine, and Homarr's Beszel widget isn't connected.
- There is no view of container CPU and memory, and no way to reach a container tool such as ctop.
- Settings does little. Backups can only be reached through the Project menu or the CLI.
- The Project folder `~/self-host` clutters the home folder.

## Solution

- **Project folder:** the Project moves to `~/.self-host`.
- **Recipes:** picking a Recipe picks its Apps visibly, so the person sees what will run and can untick any of them.
- **Pre-boot screen:** approving the plan in Onboarding opens a new animated, multi-colour full-screen scene while the images download. It shows the overall progress, invites the person to grab a coffee, and offers keys for Ko-fi and GitHub Sponsors. When the pull ends, it transitions into Activity to watch Setup and Links.
- **Where step:** it explains every choice in plain words, with a live explanation and a diagram for Exposure, plus a longer help page on `?`. Settings reuses the same explanations.
- **Remote access:** the options appear as dimmed "coming soon" entries.
- **App addresses:** they become terminal hyperlinks.
- **Beszel:** it installs an agent for this machine as well. The agent reads Docker only through a read-only socket proxy and connects to the hub automatically. Its Homarr Link adds the Beszel integration and a System Stats widget.
- **Container usage:** the containers sub-tab shows CPU and memory bars per container.
- **Settings:** it becomes five sub-tabs: Host, Appearance, Backups, Tools and About.
  - **Backups:** lists archives, backs up with an optional passphrase, and restores.
  - **Tools:** runs ctop or lazydocker when they are installed.
  - **About:** the version, the Project folder, updates and the donation keys.

## User Stories

1. As a person setting up self-host, I want my Project kept in `~/.self-host`, so that my home folder stays tidy.
2. As a person picking Apps in Onboarding, I want ticking a Recipe to tick its Apps in the list, so that I see exactly which Apps will run.
3. As a person picking a Recipe, I want to untick some of its Apps, so that I install only the ones I want.
4. As a person scanning the What list, I want a Recipe's mark to show whether all, some or none of its Apps are picked (✓ ◐ ○), so that its state matches the Apps below it.
5. As a person picking in the Catalog tab, I want picking a Recipe to behave exactly as it does in Onboarding, so that the two lists never surprise me.
6. As a person who just approved the plan, I want a pre-boot screen with motion graphics while images download, so that the wait feels like a launch rather than a stall.
7. As a person waiting on the pre-boot screen, I want to see an overall bar, "3 of 7 images" and one plain line saying what is happening, so that I know it's progressing.
8. As a person waiting, I want to be told I can go grab a coffee, so that I know I don't need to watch.
9. As a person who likes the project, I want `c` to open Ko-fi and `s` to open GitHub Sponsors in my browser, so that supporting it is one key away.
10. As a person, I want the pre-boot screen to hand over to Activity with a transition when the pull ends, so that I see Setup, credentials and Links happen live.
11. As a curious person, I want `enter` to skip from pre-boot straight to Activity, so that I can watch the details whenever I want.
12. As a person whose pull fails, I want pre-boot to end at once and land on Activity with the failure shown, so that I'm never shown a celebration of a failure.
13. As a person whose images are already on the machine, I want pre-boot to still play briefly, so that the hand-over looks the same every time.
14. As a person using `NO_COLOR`, a light terminal or a small window, I want pre-boot to stay readable, so that the effect never hides the progress.
15. As a person installing from the Catalog later, I want no pre-boot screen, so that day-to-day Actions stay quick.
16. As a person answering Where, I want a plain explanation of the highlighted Exposure choice, so that I understand who can open my Apps.
17. As a person answering Where, I want a small diagram that changes with the Exposure choice, so that I see where my Apps can be reached from.
18. As a person who wants more detail, I want `?` to open a longer help page for the current step, so that I can learn without leaving Onboarding.
19. As a person typing a password or a folder, I want `?` to type a question mark, so that help never eats my input.
20. As a person answering Where, I want every field (LAN address, time zone, user and group IDs, folders) to say in one line why it's asked, so that no question is a mystery.
21. As a person changing Exposure later in Settings, I want the same explanations and the same `?` help page, so that Settings and Onboarding agree.
22. As a person who wants remote access, I want to see Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel and HTTPS with a reverse proxy listed as "coming soon", so that I know they're planned.
23. As a person reading a coming-soon option, I want to learn what it will do without being able to pick it, so that I'm never left half-configured.
24. As a person on the Overview, the Apps list or App details, I want to cmd+click an App address in my terminal, so that I can open it the way I open any link.
25. As a person installing Beszel, I want an agent for this machine installed and connected automatically, so that Beszel shows this machine with no clicks.
26. As a security-minded person, I want the Beszel agent to read Docker only through a proxy that allows reading containers, so that it can't change them.
27. As a person who runs Homarr and Beszel, I want Homarr to show Beszel's System Stats for this machine, so that my dashboard shows its health.
28. As a person looking at an App's containers, I want CPU and memory bars per container, so that I see what's busy.
29. As a person reading the usage bars, I want CPU to be measured against the whole machine and memory against the container's limit, or the machine's memory when there is none, with the MiB used shown, so that the bars are honest.
30. As a person, I want usage to update only while the containers sub-tab is on screen, so that self-host costs nothing when I'm not looking.
31. As a person, I want Settings split into Host, Appearance, Backups, Tools and About sub-tabs on `[`/`]`, so that I can find each part quickly.
32. As a person, I want Backups to list my archives with date, size and whether each is encrypted, so that I know what I can restore.
33. As a person, I want to back up now from Settings with an optional, hidden passphrase, so that I can encrypt a backup without the CLI.
34. As a person, I want to restore the whole Project or one App from a chosen archive, with a second confirmation and a passphrase prompt only when the archive is encrypted, so that restoring is deliberate and simple.
35. As a person, I want no way to delete archives from the TUI, so that a slip can't destroy my backups.
36. As a person who uses ctop or lazydocker, I want Settings → Tools to run them with `enter` and come back afterwards, so that I can reach them from self-host.
37. As a person without those tools, I want to see the install command for my platform with `c` to copy it, so that I can add them myself; self-host never installs them.
38. As a person, I want Settings → About to show the version, the Project folder and update status, plus the Ko-fi and Sponsors keys, so that this information has one home.
39. As a person reading Help, I want the Ko-fi and Sponsors links shown as clickable links, so that I can find them there too.
40. As a visitor to the GitHub repo, I want a Sponsor button, so that I can support the project from GitHub.
41. As a script or agent using the CLI, I want `--json`, non-TTY output, `status --json` and `doctor --json` unchanged, so that my integrations keep working.

## Implementation Decisions

### Project folder

- `project.DirName` becomes `.self-host` (`internal/project/project.go:26`).
- There is no fallback to `~/self-host` and no migration, because nothing is deployed yet.
- The same change goes into:
  - the hard-coded join in `internal/clitest/clitest.go:68`;
  - every `~/self-host` mention in `internal/skill/guide.md`, `README.md`, `internal/cli/backup.go`'s help, the comment in `internal/service/service.go`, `PLAN.md` and `docs/catalog/traps/wud.md`.
- What stays as it is:
  - The Compose project name stays `self-host`.
  - `MEDIA_ROOT` and `DOWNLOADS_ROOT` stay `~/media` and `~/downloads`, outside the Project.
  - Backups follow the Project, to `~/.self-host/backups`.
  - `SELF_HOST_HOME` still overrides the folder.
- No reference outside `new-cli/` uses this path.

### Recipes

- A Recipe carries only `Apps []string` (`internal/catalog/catalog.go:10-15`). So picking it is purely a shortcut for its Apps.
- In Onboarding What and in the Catalog tab (`internal/tui/install.go`, `picked`):
  - Picking a Recipe picks its Apps, and unpicking it unpicks them.
  - A Recipe's mark is derived from its Apps: ✓ all picked, ◐ some, ○ none.
  - The plan installs the picked Apps; `expand()` in `onboarding.go` already expands Recipes.
- huh's MultiSelect has no derived marks. A small custom list in What is acceptable if it keeps #139's live description of the hovered entry, the scrolling and the 80-column fit.

### Pre-boot screen

- **When it plays:**
  - A new full-screen surface sits between approving at Review and the Dashboard, for Onboarding's first install only.
  - It plays while the install Action pulls images, then plays an exit transition and lands on the Dashboard with Activity focused. That is today's hand-over, made later.
- **What it shows:** progress from the same Activity snapshot as Activity and the Now strip: the overall pull bar, "N of M images" and the narrative line. No new model state, and per-image bars stay in Activity. The message invites the person to grab a coffee.
- **Edge cases:**
  - A failed pull ends pre-boot at once and lands on Activity, with no transition.
  - When there is nothing to pull, pre-boot still plays for about 4 s, then transitions.
- **Keys:** `enter` skips to Activity, `c` opens https://ko-fi.com/ajnart, `s` opens https://github.com/sponsors/ajnart, and `q` behaves as on the Dashboard. Opening a page uses `Backend.OpenURL`, which runs `open` or `xdg-open`.
- **Look:** a parallax starfield, twinkling sparkles, and the ◆ brand pulsing with a colour sweep through purple, pink, cyan and gold. The exit transition stretches the stars into warp streaks, then wipes in the Dashboard. The progress bar is still a bar, never a percentage.
- **Exceptions, on this screen only:**
  - It may use several colours instead of the single accent, with dark and light variants.
  - It animates at 24 fps instead of 12, and ticks only while it is on screen.
- **Fallbacks:** under `NO_COLOR` it shows the same motion in monochrome. Below 80×24 it draws a simpler scene and never cuts the text.
- **Rendering:** the scene is a pure renderer (frame, width, height, progress, palette → lines), like seam 2, so fixed frames can be golden-tested.
- **Order of work:** a throwaway prototype comes first, with 2–3 variants shown as animated previews; the maintainer picks one, and only then is it built for real.

### Where explanations and help

- **What Exposure actually does:**
  - `lan` publishes App ports on `0.0.0.0`, so any device that can reach this machine on the network can open them.
  - `local` publishes them on `127.0.0.1`, so only this computer can.
  - `LAN_IP` only builds App links (`service.go:106-167`). The explanations must say exactly this.
- **Live explanation:** under the highlighted Exposure choice. Draft wording:
  - "Phones, TVs and laptops on the same Wi-Fi or router as this computer can open your Apps at 192.168.1.20. Nobody on the internet can."
  - "Your Apps open only in a browser on this computer. Other devices can't reach them."
- **Diagram:** a small one that changes with the choice: the devices, then the router, then this computer, with "internet ✗".
- **Other fields:** every Where field gets a one-line live explanation: LAN address, time zone, user and group IDs, media and downloads folders.
- **`?` help page:**
  - It opens the current step's longer help page wherever the focus is not on a free-text input. Inside a text input, `?` types a question mark.
  - `esc` or `?` closes it.
  - The bar shows a `? more` chip only where it works.
- **Exposure help page contents:**
  - a larger diagram;
  - what a LAN address is and where it comes from;
  - that nobody on the internet can reach the Apps unless port forwarding is set up on the router;
  - that a firewall may need a rule;
  - that everything can be changed later in Settings.
- **Settings:** the EXPOSURE row reuses the same explanation and the same `?` page.

### Coming-soon remote access

- Exposure lists three entries after `lan` and `local`, dimmed and marked "coming soon": Tailscale (your devices, from anywhere), Cloudflare Tunnel (a public address) and HTTPS with a reverse proxy (Caddy).
- The highlight can land on them and shows what they will do. `enter` says "coming soon" and selects nothing.
- Persisted `EXPOSURE` values stay `lan` and `local`.
- Caddy, Traefik, Nginx Proxy Manager, Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel are already Catalog Apps. Routing Apps through them is a later spec, and the repo's ingress rules apply then: one owner for DNS, TLS and ports 80/443, and public access only as a separate approval.

### Clickable addresses

- Every App address on the Overview, the Apps list and App details is wrapped with `ansi.SetHyperlink(fullURL, visibleText)`. The visible text and the width calculation stay unchanged, and `o` still works.
- The TUI uses `tea.MouseModeCellMotion` (`view.go:521`), so a terminal may need a modifier key for cmd+click.
- The maintainer checks it in their terminal. If it doesn't work there, the change is dropped.

### Beszel agent

- The Beszel App (`internal/apps/beszel/beszel.go`, hub `henrygd/beszel:0.20.0`, no agent today) gains two services:
  - **Agent:** `henrygd/beszel-agent` at the hub's version.
  - **Socket proxy:** the read-only proxy Beszel documents (LinuxServer's socket-proxy, with container reads only, `CONTAINERS=1`, and writes denied). It is the only service that mounts `/var/run/docker.sock`.
- **How the agent connects:**
  - It uses WebSocket mode (v0.12+), with `HUB_URL` set to the hub on `127.0.0.1`, a `TOKEN` and the hub's public `KEY`.
  - It runs with `network_mode: host` and `LISTEN=127.0.0.1:45876`.
  - It reaches the proxy on a port published on `127.0.0.1` whatever the Exposure, through `DOCKER_HOST`.
- **New Setup steps, after `ready` and `admin-login`:**
  1. Get the hub's public key.
  2. Get a permanent universal token with `GET /api/beszel/universal-token?enable=1&permanent=1`, signed in as the Admin login user.
  3. Write the agent's settings to the Project's secrets.
  4. Start the agent.
  5. Check that this machine appears as a system.
- Every Check probes afresh, because `h.Step` re-runs Check after Do.
- `tools/appgen` rejects socket mounts, and e2e isolation flags them. Both gain one named exception for this proxy service only. `docs/catalog/traps/beszel.md` records it.
- Verify every image name, environment variable and API route against the Beszel docs at implementation time.

### Beszel → Homarr Link

- A new target in `internal/apps/homarr/links.go`, following the qBittorrent pattern:
  - the Homarr integration kind for Beszel;
  - the username `<AdminUser>@selfhost.local` and the Admin password;
  - one "Beszel System Stats" widget bound to this machine's system.
- The App tile, the integration and the widget remain three separate claims.
- Homarr's Beszel integration exists since 1.65.0. The catalog runs `ghcr.io/homarr-labs/homarr:dev`.

### Container usage

- **Data:**
  - A new streaming Backend method reads `docker stats` for the Project's containers.
  - It runs only while the Apps tab's containers sub-tab is on screen, using the same lifecycle as the log stream: started and stopped from `syncLogs`'s place in `Model.Update`.
  - `service.ContainerStatus` and `status --json` stay unchanged.
- **Bars:**
  - CPU fraction is CPU% ÷ (100 × host cores).
  - Memory fraction is usage ÷ limit; Docker reports the machine's memory as the limit when there is none.
  - The text says "312 MiB", never a percentage.
  - Everything fits 80 columns.

### Settings sub-tabs

- **Sub-tabs:** Host · Appearance · Backups · Tools · About, switched with `[`/`]` (ADR 0004's sub-tab keys).
  - `tab` moves pane focus inside a sub-tab.
  - Host settings and Appearance move into their own sub-tabs.
  - ADR 0004 and `TestKeybindAudit` are updated.
- **Backups:**
  - **The list:** archives in `<Project>/backups/selfhost-*.tar.zst`, with date, size and whether each is encrypted.
  - **Back up now:** `b` asks for an optional passphrase (hidden; empty means none), then runs the backup Action. `Service.Backup` already takes a passphrase; `ServiceBackend.Run` passes `""` today.
  - **Restore:** `enter` on an archive opens a restore preview: the whole Project or one App, from the archive's manifest. It asks for the passphrase only when the archive is encrypted, needs a second `enter`, and runs `Service.Restore(file, ids, passphrase)` as an Action in Activity.
  - **No delete.**
- **Tools:**
  - **Detection:** looks for `ctop` and `lazydocker` on `PATH`.
  - **Installed:** `enter` runs the tool with `tea.ExecProcess`. Nothing suspends the TUI today, so this is new.
  - **Missing:** the tool is dimmed, with its install command for this platform and `c` to copy it. Verify the commands at implementation time.
  - self-host never installs a tool.
- **About:**
  - shows the version, the Project folder and update status (the existing release check);
  - `c` opens Ko-fi and `s` opens Sponsors;
  - the links are also hyperlinks.

### Donation links

- `.github/FUNDING.yml` contains `github: ajnart` and `ko_fi: ajnart`. Both pages exist.
- Help shows both URLs as hyperlinks, with no keys of its own.
- The keys exist only on the pre-boot screen and in Settings → About.

### Unchanged

`--json`, non-TTY output, `status --json`, `doctor --json`, persisted formats (`.env`, `state.json`, `appearance.json`) and the semantics of backend Actions all stay as they are.

## Testing Decisions

- **TUI tests:** they use #129's seams only:
  1. the Activity model;
  2. pure renderers, including the pre-boot scene, golden-tested at fixed frames and ANSI-stripped, plus one styled assertion for `NO_COLOR`;
  3. views plus the Model harness, with goldens at 120×30 and 80×24, `TestEveryViewFitsEightyColumns` and `TestKeybindAudit`.
- **Test style:** test-first, one behaviour at a time. Tests assert what a person sees or which Action is dispatched. Expected values come from literals or worked examples.
- **App changes:** the Beszel agent, the proxy and the Homarr Link use the existing App test patterns: fragment, Setup, Check and Link tests like `internal/apps/homarr/homarr_test.go`, plus the appgen rule tests.
- **Service and Backend additions:** stats and listing archives are tested with the existing fakes. No Docker.
- **Excluded:** no Docker, e2e runtime, browser or installer runs. The pre-boot prototype is throwaway and never committed.

## Out of Scope

- Routing Apps through Caddy, Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel (a later spec).
- Named Docker volumes for App configuration: dropped for now. Abdullah's reason is still to be asked.
- Ports and disk host checks in Onboarding (#140).
- Monitoring other machines with Beszel.
- Usage history (Beszel provides that).
- Deleting or scheduling backups from the TUI.
- Installing optional tools.
- A pre-boot screen for Catalog installs.

## Further Notes

- **CI is blocked:** GitHub Actions does not start jobs: _"recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased"_. Until billing is fixed, each ticket's PR is merged on local gates:
  - gofmt, `go vet ./...` and `go vet -tags e2e ./e2e/`;
  - `go test ./...` and `go test -race` on `internal/activity` and `internal/tui`;
  - the four `CGO_ENABLED=0` cross-builds.

  After that, CI is required again.

- **Delivery:** one PR per ticket into `main`, merged with a merge commit after a clean review. The previous work landed in PR #31 (`a673df7d`).

## Decision needed

Spec #129 (story 63) and ticket #138 ask Onboarding's Initializing step to check "Docker, Compose, ports and disk" before the person chooses anything. Doctor (`internal/host`, `internal/service/doctor.go`) does not check ports or disk on a machine without a Project. It checks only Docker, the Docker daemon, Docker Compose and container IDs, plus the firewall and Exposure checks once a Project exists.

Adding ports and disk checks to Doctor would add new checks to `self-host doctor` and `doctor --json`. Spec #129 says `--json` output must not change, so Onboarding shipped with the existing checks only (#138).

## Options

1. Add `disk` (free space under the Project folder) and `ports` (the chosen Apps' ports are free) checks to Doctor. `doctor --json` gains new check entries but keeps its format: an additive change, but still a change.
2. Run the ports and disk checks only inside the TUI's Onboarding, through a new read-only `Backend` method, so `doctor` and `--json` stay as they are. Two places then know about host checks.
3. Keep today's behaviour. Port conflicts are already caught per App at install time (preflight), and disk is not checked.

## Where it would land

- Onboarding: `internal/tui/onboarding.go`, the Initializing step, which reveals whatever checks it receives.
- Doctor: `internal/host`, `internal/service/doctor.go`.
