body:
## Problem Statement

The self-host TUI works but does not feel like a place to work. It opens on a Dashboard that lists Apps and a few panels, and every other surface (Stack, Workflow, Install, Settings) is a separate full-screen view reached by a letter key. Single keys start, stop or take down Apps and the whole Project with no preview, so a stray key changes things. When an Action runs after Onboarding, all a person sees is one footer line with a spinner and text such as "pulling 7 images · 56% · 225 MB/400 MB"; the Workflow view only shows the steps if they go looking. Image pulls are reported as percentages and megabytes (per layer in the plain CLI), not as progress you can read at a glance. Nothing animates except one small spinner, so it is hard to tell what is happening, what finished, and what is waiting. The first-run wizard asks the right things but explains little, and installs inside its own screen instead of handing over to the place the person will keep using. Colours are approximations, focus is not obvious, and inactive and active elements look alike.

## Solution

The Dashboard becomes a command center in the spirit of Zellij (ADR 0004): five tabs — Overview, Apps, Activity, Catalog, Settings — on `1`–`5` and `←`/`→`, with an always-visible bottom bar that shows the global keys and the focused pane's keys as chips. No single key changes anything: `a` opens the Action menu for the selected App and `A` for the Project; the menu shows only the Actions valid now, previews what the highlighted one will do, and runs it only on `enter`. Only read-only actions keep direct keys (open, copy a credential, search, go into an App, help).

Every Action is presented as it happens. The Activity tab takes focus when an Action starts and shows its stages with animation: one overall bar plus slim per-image bars while pulling, a spinner that turns into a pulsing green dot when a container starts, Setup steps that run visibly one at a time and turn into ✓, credentials shown as masked dots filling in, Links drawn as a dashed line that fills into an arrow, a green wave when it all finishes, and one narrative line that says in plain words what is happening now. The Overview mirrors the running Action in a small "Now" strip. Progress is shown with bars, never percentages; small dim facts ("2 of 3 images") are allowed. The interactive terminal output of the CLI uses the same presentation; `--json` and non-terminal output stay plain.

Onboarding is redesigned as a seven-step setup wizard that explains why it asks each thing: an animated host check, a welcome, what to run, where it lives (folders and Exposure in plain words), who administers it (the Admin login), how it should look (Nerd Font icons or simple symbols), and a review to approve. Approving hands over to the Dashboard with Activity focused, where the first Action comes to life.

The look is a purple accent (around #7A57D3) on near-black surfaces with green and red reserved for states and amber for attention, and a clear hierarchy through weight and brightness: what is active is bold and near-white, what is inactive is normal-weight grey, and the focused pane has a purple border and bold title.

## User Stories

1. As a person opening self-host, I want five tabs I can reach with `1`–`5`, so that every surface is one key away.
2. As a person, I want `←`/`→` to move between tabs, so that I can browse without remembering numbers.
3. As a person, I want the active tab to be bold and bright and the others grey, so that I always know where I am.
4. As a person, I want `↑`/`↓` to move only within the focused list, so that arrows never mean two things.
5. As a person, I want `tab` to move focus between panes inside a tab, so that I can reach the detail pane without the mouse.
6. As a person, I want `[` and `]` to switch sub-tabs inside a pane (logs, Setup, info, compose, containers), so that sub-tabs do not collide with tab switching.
7. As a person, I want the focused pane to have a purple border and a bold title and unfocused panes to be grey, so that my attention lands on the right place.
8. As a person, I want an always-visible bottom bar with global keys on the left and the focused pane's keys as chips on the right, so that I never have to guess what I can press.
9. As a person, I want the bottom bar to change with the focused pane, so that it only shows keys that do something here.
10. As a person, I want `?` to show every key with its meaning, so that I can learn the tool.
11. As a person, I want no single key to start, stop, update or remove an App, so that a stray key never changes my server.
12. As a person, I want `a` to open the Action menu for the selected App, so that every change starts from one place.
13. As a person, I want the Action menu to list only the Actions valid in the App's current state, so that I am not offered impossible choices.
14. As a person, I want each Action in the menu to have a mnemonic letter that moves the highlight, so that `a` then `u` gets me to Update quickly.
15. As a person, I want the highlighted Action to show a one-line preview of what it will do, so that I know the consequences before confirming.
16. As a person, I want an Action to run only when I press `enter`, so that previewing is always safe.
17. As a person, I want destructive Actions (stop, remove, down) to be red and need a second `enter`, so that I do not lose work by accident.
18. As a person, I want `esc` to close the Action menu without doing anything, so that I can back out at any time.
19. As a person, I want `A` to open the Action menu for the whole Project (up all, down all, restart all, update all, backup), so that Project-wide control lives in one menu.
20. As a person, I want unavailable Actions such as Update with no update known to be shown greyed with the reason, so that I understand why I cannot use them.
21. As a person, I want `o` to open the selected App in my browser, so that the most common read-only action stays one key.
22. As a person, I want `c` to open a picker of the selected App's credentials (Admin password, login alias, API keys) and copy the one I choose, so that I never see secrets I did not ask for.
23. As a person, I want `/` to search the focused list, so that I can find an App among dozens.
24. As a person, I want `enter` on an App in Overview to take me to the Apps tab with that App focused, so that going deeper is natural.
25. As a person, I want the Overview to show every App with its Status, category and Setup state at a glance, so that I know if everything is fine in one look.
26. As a person, I want a Needs attention panel listing failed steps, Manual steps, updates and host warnings, each with the exact chord that resolves it, so that I know what to do next.
27. As a person, I want a Now strip on the Overview that mirrors the running Action with its bar and narrative, so that I can stay on the Overview while something runs.
28. As a person, I want the Now strip to show the last Action's result and host health when nothing runs, so that the Overview is never empty.
29. As a person, I want the header to show the Project, LAN address, overall health and time, so that I have context without looking for it.
30. As a person, I want the Apps tab to show the selected App's details in sub-tabs including its containers and images, so that everything about one App is together.
31. As a person, I want Project-wide controls to be reachable from the Apps tab through `A`, so that I do not need a separate Stack view.
32. As a person, I want the Activity tab to take focus when an Action starts, so that I see it happen without navigating.
33. As a person, I want to switch away from Activity while an Action runs and come back, so that a long pull does not lock me in.
34. As a person, I want Activity to show the running or most recent Action at the top and every App's remembered steps below, so that I can see both now and the overall state.
35. As a person watching a pull, I want one overall bar for all images of the Action, so that I know how far the whole download is.
36. As a person watching a pull, I want a slim bar per image, so that I can see which image is slow.
37. As a person, I want no percentages, only bars and small dim facts like "2 of 3 images", so that progress reads at a glance.
38. As a person, I want image sizes only in details or logs, so that the main view stays calm.
39. As a person watching a container start, I want a spinner that turns into a green dot that pulses once when it is running, so that I notice the moment it comes up.
40. As a person watching Setup, I want steps to run visibly one at a time, each with a spinner that turns into ✓ and its message, so that I can follow the order.
41. As a person, I want a failed step to turn into ✗ with its error and hint, so that I know exactly what went wrong and how to fix it.
42. As a person, I want a Manual step to show as needing me, with its hint, distinct from a failure, so that I know it is my turn, not a bug.
43. As a person watching credentials being created, I want masked dots filling in and a "saved" chip, so that I see it happen without ever seeing the secret.
44. As a person watching a Link, I want a dashed line between the two Apps that fills and grows into an arrow when the Link applies, so that I see Apps being wired together.
45. As a person, I want a Link waiting for its target to stay dashed and grey with "waiting for …", so that I understand why it has not run.
46. As a person, I want a green wave down the App rows when the Action finishes, so that I feel the moment everything is ready.
47. As a person, I want one narrative line at the bottom of Activity that says in plain words what is happening now, so that I understand without reading every row.
48. As a person, I want the final state of a finished Action to stay visible until the next one, so that I can read what happened.
49. As a person, I want counters such as "3/7 Apps set up" and "Links 2/4" next to box titles, so that I see progress per kind of work.
50. As a person, I want animations only while something is running, so that an idle Dashboard does not flicker or use CPU.
51. As a person, I want animations to run at about 12 frames per second, so that they look smooth without being distracting.
52. As a person running `self-host install` in a terminal, I want the same bars, spinners and step states as the TUI, so that the CLI feels like the same product.
53. As an agent or CI job, I want `--json` and non-terminal output to stay plain, stable and free of animation, so that my parsing never breaks.
54. As a person with `NO_COLOR` set, I want the UI to stay readable without colour, so that every state is still clear from its glyph.
55. As a person, I want every state to have a glyph as well as a colour, so that colour is never the only signal.
56. As a person on a light terminal, I want a light theme built from the same roles, so that the UI is readable everywhere.
57. As a person, I want the purple accent around #7A57D3 used for focus, selection and progress, so that the brand colour guides my eye.
58. As a person, I want green and red used only for states and amber for attention, so that colours always mean the same thing.
59. As a person with a Nerd Font, I want App category icons and Docker, key and link stage icons, so that the UI is richer.
60. As a person without a Nerd Font, I want simple Unicode symbols instead, so that nothing renders as boxes.
61. As a person, I want bars, spinners and state dots to look the same with or without Nerd Fonts, so that progress never depends on fonts.
62. As a person, I want to change the glyph choice later in Settings, so that I can switch after installing a font.
63. As a first-time person, I want Onboarding to start with an animated check of Docker, Compose, ports and disk, so that I know my machine is ready before I choose anything.
64. As a first-time person, I want each failed host check to show a fix hint and a recheck, so that I can repair it without leaving.
65. As a first-time person, I want a welcome step that says what self-host will do and that nothing is written until I approve, so that I feel safe continuing.
66. As a first-time person, I want to pick Recipes and Apps with live descriptions, so that I know what I am choosing.
67. As a first-time person, I want the folders and Exposure explained in plain words ("other devices on your network can open these at …"), so that I understand where things live and who can reach them.
68. As a first-time person, I want to choose or generate the shared Admin login, so that I know how I will sign in to every App.
69. As a first-time person, I want a sample line of icons and a question "Do these icons look right?", so that I pick the glyph style that works on my terminal.
70. As a first-time person, I want a link to learn about Nerd Fonts, so that I can install one if I want the icons.
71. As a first-time person, I want to be asked only for inputs the chosen Apps need, so that Onboarding stays short.
72. As a first-time person, I want a step indicator at the top and `esc` to go back, so that I always know where I am and can change my mind.
73. As a first-time person, I want a review of the plan as a table before anything is written, so that I approve exactly what will happen.
74. As a first-time person, I want approving to hand me over to the Dashboard with Activity focused, so that I watch my Apps come to life in the place I will keep using.
75. As a first-time person, I want a short initializing screen while Onboarding loads, so that the first frame is not a blank terminal.
76. As a person in a narrow terminal (80×24), I want panes to stack and bars to shrink, so that the UI stays usable.
77. As a person, I want long names and messages truncated with "…", so that rows never wrap and break the layout.
78. As a person, I want the mouse to select Apps, tabs and menu entries, so that I can use the TUI either way.
79. As a maintainer, I want the keybind audit to check ADR 0004, so that the key model cannot drift silently.

## Implementation Decisions

- The key model and tab layout follow ADR 0004 (tabbed command center with action chords), which supersedes ADR 0002. Glossary terms used: Dashboard, Overview tab, Apps tab, Activity, Catalog, Settings, Action, Action menu, Needs attention, Onboarding, App details, Keybind.
- The existing Dashboard, Stack, Workflow, Install and Settings views are reorganised into five tabs: Overview (Apps with Status, Needs attention, Now strip, header), Apps (App details sub-tabs plus containers and images from Stack), Activity (Workflow plus the running Action), Catalog (the Install view), Settings (Host settings plus Appearance). The Stack and Workflow views stop being separate surfaces.
- Keys: `1`–`5` and `←`/`→` switch tabs; `↑`/`↓` move in the focused list; `tab` moves pane focus; `[`/`]` switch sub-tabs; `a` App Action menu; `A` Project Action menu; `o` open; `c` credential picker; `/` search; `enter` go into the selected App (Overview jumps to Apps; Apps focuses the detail pane); `?` help; `q` quit. No single key changes an App or the Project. Stack's `1`/`2`/`3` Project controls move into the `A` menu.
- The Action menu is a new view-level component: it receives the selected App's state (or the Project's) and lists only valid Actions, each with a mnemonic, a one-line preview and a destructive flag; typing a mnemonic moves the highlight, `enter` runs (twice for destructive), `esc` closes. It dispatches the existing backend Actions (start, stop, restart, update, retry Setup, remove, up, down, restart all, update all, backup).
- The existing pure Workflow module is deepened into the Activity model: input is the Project status plus task events; output is a presentation snapshot of the running or most recent Action — ordered stages (pull, start, Setup, credentials, Links, check) with their state, an overall pull fraction across all images and a fraction per image, per-App step rows (states: done, skipped, failed, manual, running, not run), Link rows (source, target, state, waiting reason), counters (Apps set up, Links applied, images pulled), the narrative line, and a "finished" marker — followed by every App's remembered steps. It stays pure (no I/O, no clock).
- Pull progress aggregation computes totals across all images of the Action (known bytes per image, images done count), replacing per-layer reporting in the plain CLI and the percentage text everywhere.
- A single pure presentation renderer turns a snapshot into text: input is the snapshot, an animation frame number, a width and a glyph set; output is styled lines. Bars use a rounded, cell-based style with a track; spinners use braille frames; transitions (dot pulse on start, Link line filling into an arrow, masked dots filling in, finish wave) are expressed as functions of the frame since the stage changed. The renderer has no knowledge of Bubble Tea and is used by both the Activity tab / Now strip and the interactive CLI output.
- Animation ticking: the TUI and the interactive CLI drive frames at about 12 fps only while an Action runs or a transition is still playing; ticking stops when idle. There is no reduced-motion mode.
- Interactive CLI output (a TTY) redraws a compact block in place using the renderer; non-TTY and `--json` output keep today's plain line and JSON events unchanged.
- Theme: a new palette with the primary accent around #7A57D3 (exact values chosen during implementation), near-black surfaces, a grey text hierarchy, green and red reserved for states, amber for attention, info blue for neutral chips, and a light theme derived from the same roles (the existing light/dark background detection is kept). Hierarchy through weight and brightness: active or focused text is bold and near-white, inactive is normal-weight grey, disabled is faint. `NO_COLOR` is honoured; every state also has a glyph.
- Glyph sets: two sets, "Nerd Font" and "Simple". Nerd Font icons are used only where they carry meaning (App category icons in the Apps list, Docker/key/link stage icons in Activity, the brand mark); bars, spinners and state dots are identical in both sets. The choice is a non-secret appearance setting stored with the Project and editable in Settings; Onboarding sets it.
- Onboarding replaces the current wizard with seven steps: Initializing (animated host checks with fix hints and recheck), Welcome, What (Recipes and Apps), Where (folders and Exposure in plain words), Who (Admin login), Look (glyph sample, Nerd Fonts link, choice), Review (plan table and approve). A step indicator sits at the top; `esc` goes back; inputs are asked only when the chosen Apps need them. Approving creates the Project and starts the install Action, then hands over to the Dashboard with Activity focused; the wizard's own Installing screen is removed.
- The App-level first-administrator helpers are named firstadmin (already renamed) so Onboarding refers only to the person's wizard.
- Status strings in persisted state and `status --json` do not change; the UI reads the named step and Setup states.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests exercise external behaviour through the agreed seams only: given inputs, assert what a person would see or what Action is dispatched; never assert internal fields, private helpers or styling internals. Each behaviour is driven test-first (red, green, refactor).
- Seam 1 — Activity model (pure): table-driven tests from Project status plus task events to the snapshot: stage order, overall and per-image pull fractions (including images with unknown size and images finishing out of order), step and Link states including manual and waiting, counters, narrative line, reset on a new run, finished marker. Prior art: the existing Workflow module tests and pull aggregation tests.
- Seam 2 — Presentation renderer (pure): frame goldens at fixed frames for each stage (pull bars at several fractions, start pulse, Setup spinner to ✓, masked credentials, Link dashed→filled→arrow, finish wave), both glyph sets, widths 120 and 80, with and without colour. Prior art: the TUI golden files and their `-update` flow.
- Seam 3 — Views and Model harness: isolated view tests (small view context plus fake backend) for tab switching by number and arrows, pane focus and sub-tabs, Action menu (valid entries per state, mnemonic highlight, preview text, enter runs, destructive double enter, esc cancels, Project menu), read-only direct keys, Activity taking focus when an Action starts, Overview Now strip, Onboarding steps (back, step indicator, only-needed inputs, glyph choice persisted, approve hands over to Activity). Model-level goldens at 120×30 and 80×24 for every tab and Onboarding step; the 80-column fit check; the keybind audit rewritten against ADR 0004. Prior art: the existing views tests, harness tests, goldens and keybind audit.
- The interactive CLI output is tested through the renderer plus a sink test that a TTY sink redraws the block and a non-TTY sink prints today's plain lines unchanged; `--json` output is covered by the existing CLI tests and must not change.
- No Docker, e2e or browser runs are needed for this work.

## Out of Scope

- Reduced-motion mode.
- Zellij-style modal keybindings.
- A persisted history of past Actions (Activity shows the running or most recent Action plus remembered steps).
- An ASCII-only glyph set.
- Changes to `--json` output, non-TTY output, persisted state formats or backend Action semantics.
- New Actions beyond those the backend already supports.
- Runtime acceptance work (#45, #50, #88), host decisions (Pi-hole/Technitium DNS port 53, PHP-FPM confinement for #66/#86) and Homarr live verification; these are parked separately.
- The marketing video itself (feat/video-reels).

## Further Notes

- Visual reference: the terminal reel on the feat/video-reels branch (video/terminal-reel) shows the intended feel — one accent, near-black surfaces, braille spinner at 12 fps, one overall bar plus counters, Apps and Links boxes, a narrative line, and sequential Setup. Its review notes reject a "too fast, too dense" cut and require masked credentials and visibly sequential Setup.
- Suggested order: (1) Activity model + renderer + Activity tab and Now strip + interactive CLI output; (2) tabbed shell, key model, bottom bar, Action menu, Overview; (3) Onboarding; (4) Apps, Catalog and Settings tabs including Appearance.
- Decisions were settled in a grilling session on 2026-10-09; the glossary (CONTEXT.md) and ADR 0004 are already committed on feat/new-cli (PR #31).
title: Spec: TUI command center — tabs, Action menu, animated Activity, redesigned Onboarding

## What to build

`go test ./...` passes on macOS as it does on Linux CI. Four tests fail only on macOS at feat/new-cli (37d4…, after the #115 merge):

- `internal/apps/netdata` `TestStartupRemovesOnlyProvenStockShortcutAndPreservesArguments`: "startup fixture: exit status 1" on every subtest. The fixture runs the startup script with the host `sh`/`cp`; BSD `cp -an` differs from busybox/GNU.
- `e2e` (untagged fixture tests) `TestAutheliaFixtureVerifiedChildTLSAndBoundedRoute` ("trusted child did not reach genuine TLS backend") and `TestNetBirdFixtureTLSRequiresOwnedCA` ("child SSL_CERT_FILE did not establish verified TLS"): Go on darwin ignores `SSL_CERT_FILE` and verifies through the system keychain.
- `e2e` `TestNetBirdDockerWrapperRestrictsOwnedSelectors` ("owned pinned backup helper rejected").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four pass on macOS and still pass on Linux.
- [ ] The fixtures still prove the real behaviour (container busybox for netdata; trusted-CA TLS for the child processes) — do not weaken the shipped script or the TLS checks; where the platform genuinely cannot express the check, skip with a reason that names the platform limit and keep the Linux path.

Any two catalog Apps can be installed in the same Project. #108 made render refuse a Compose service name defined by two Apps, but only Immich/Nextcloud Redis was renamed. Nine Apps still declare `db` (bookstack, docmost, fireflyiii, keycloak, nextcloud, paperlessngx, passbolt, seafile, umami) and five declare `redis` (docmost, mayan, patchmon, seafile, tracearr), so e.g. installing BookStack then Nextcloud now fails at render.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every App's auxiliary services carry App-owned names (e.g. `<app>-db`), and the render test proves every pair of catalog Apps renders together.
- [ ] Each App's own references (env hosts, `depends_on`, healthchecks, Setup/Check helpers, backup/restore of database files) follow the rename.
- [ ] An existing Project installed with the old names upgrades cleanly: data paths are unchanged, and the old containers are removed only within the Project (no volume deletion).
- [ ] Catalog traps note the naming rule.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Compose: give auxiliary services App-owned names so any two Apps co-install

## Concrete failure

The isolated app-seafile target on immutable revision f06f1b262c4deaca1a2d538e86bd9843ed434f2f completed install failure at 2026-10-07T13:16:19Z. Its ordinary evidence retains a ready-step timeout after ten minutes of HTTP 502; cleanup passed. This is distinct from #80's earlier harness timeout diagnostics. The selected public hostname-port repair is already present.

## Confirmed source defect

The adapter pins seafileltd/seafile-mc:13.0.28 but omits SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_CCNET_DB_NAME, SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAFILE_DB_NAME, and SEAFILE_MYSQL_DB_SEAHUB_DB_NAME. The bootstrap script extracted from the tested public image sha256:d3b8f07584d05a6cc1443bb86b48f916b452bbd49b0d6fea9f127fcf354bb490 exports each omitted name as a present empty CCNET_DB/SEAFILE_DB/SEAHUB_DB installer environment value.

The exact v13.0.28-server installer uses arg or os.environ.get(env, default), so present empty values defeat its fallback names. It rejects the first empty name with 'Incomplete mysql configuration parameters, missing ccnet db name parameter'. The official v13 Compose configuration explicitly supplies ccnet_db, seafile_db, and seahub_db. The public container entrypoint backgrounds startup and keeps an idle loop running, so container liveness does not demonstrate successful initialization. This defect can leave the proxy returning HTTP 502; the runtime retry is still required to establish that no further startup defect remains.

Primary sources:
- https://github.com/haiwen/seafile-docker/blob/master/scripts/scripts_13.0/bootstrap.py (tested image extraction confirms the three exact exports)
- https://github.com/haiwen/seahub/blob/v13.0.28-server/scripts/setup-seafile-mysql.py
- https://manual.seafile.com/13.0/setup/setup_ce_by_docker/
- https://github.com/haiwen/seafile-docker/blob/master/scripts/scripts_13.0/enterpoint.sh

## Narrow repair and validation

Declare the three official database names in the owned Seafile Compose environment. Preserve all image pins, credentials, account, binds, and existing data. No timeout extension or unrelated dependency change.

A focused public Compose regression fails before the repair for all three omitted names and passes afterward. The existing selected-public-port regression also passes. A bounded source replay of the tested image's database mapping and the exact installer parameter checks fails with the omitted names and passes with the official names, without database access or private files. No Docker acceptance or broad tests were run by the implementation agent. Real isolated install and the complete lifecycle, including restore, remain required.

Choosing PUID=0 for compatible images does not solve this image.

- New rootless Projects default container PUID/PGID to0:0 while keeping Project filesystem ownership with the invoking host user.

- Keep ordinary rootful defaults unchanged; report unknown inspection in doctor instead of asserting a known mode.

The persistent Project lock introduced by #40 must retain the invoking user's ownership and reject symlink or special-file destinations.

Concrete failures: a sudo-created root-owned mode-0644 `.lock` cannot be reopened for ordinary-user mutations; opening a pre-existing `.lock` symlink follows its target and truncates/writes the lock claim into unrelated state or files.

Acceptance:
- Open the lock descriptor without following symlinks and reject nonregular files before claiming or truncating.
- Preserve outside sentinel and state bytes when the lock path is a symlink; return an actionable error.
- Preserve the persistent inode and assign the Project owner's ownership through its descriptor when privileged.
- Focused behavioral regressions cover symlink and special-file rejection and the privileged-to-ordinary-user transition where supported.
- Existing cancellation, cross-process exclusion and replacement-path ownership regressions remain green.

Depends on #40. Required before real catalog acceptance (#45).

body:
LoadState repairs damaged state from bytes read outside the Project mutation lock. Status, Doctor and Install preflight use it too. A concurrent mutation can save newer state between that read and repair, then lose its changes to the stale recovered snapshot.

Acceptance:
- Ordinary state reads never rewrite state or recovery files; Status stays responsive during long mutations and can return the first complete salvageable value.
- Recovery is explicit under the existing Project mutation lock, rereads current bytes after acquisition, and preserves the actual damaged file privately before repair.
- A reader cannot overwrite a newer writer; unrecoverable corruption reports useful recovery instructions without claiming a copy was written when it was not.
- Public Project/service regressions prove read-only salvage, repair on the next mutation, preservation of concurrent changes and corruption-copy mode.

Dependencies: #40 and #47. Part of PR #31 persistence/recovery audit.
title: Project: recover damaged state only under the mutation lock

body:
First Install writes Host settings before the shared Project mutation lock and resolves remembered App inputs before entering it. A canceled first install can still create the Project; concurrent installs can overwrite each other's Host choices or newly saved inputs. Fresh Restore also writes .env before locking and decides whether to replace shared credentials from a pre-lock existence check.

Acceptance:
- First Project initialization occurs under the same cancellable mutation lock as later edits.
- Cancelled first Install/Restore leaves no active Project settings or App mutations.
- Inputs are resolved against the session loaded while holding the lock, preserving concurrent changes to unrelated inputs.
- Fresh Restore restores global credentials only if it actually initialized the Project under lock; an existing Project preserves its Admin login/unrelated App secrets.
- Focused service/CLI regressions exercise cancellation, competing first runs and queued input changes at public operation boundaries.

Dependencies: #40 and #41. Part of PR #31 release-readiness audit.

Acceptance:

body:
Restore can delete original App data when a replacement directory is missing or its rename fails: it moves the original into staging then unconditionally deletes staging. Restoring every App in a scoped backup also replaces secrets belonging to unrelated Apps. Backup ignores Docker Ps errors and uses a cancelled context to restart stopped Apps.

Acceptance:
- Validate every selected replacement before touching Apps; failed restore preserves/rolls back original directories and records, with a recoverable path if rollback itself fails.
- Existing-Project restores preserve unrelated App secrets and shared Admin login; fresh whole-backup recovery restores its own credentials.
- Unknown container state fails backup before copying live data.
- Originally running services are restarted with a bounded recovery context on failure/cancellation; report archive and restart failures.
- Focused CLI/service regressions cover malformed backup, scoped restore, Ps failure and cancellation recovery.

Dependencies: archive-extraction containment must pass before runtime restore acceptance. Part of PR #31 release audit.

body:
Project locking can steal a live claim between exclusive file creation and PID write. Stale lock read/unlink/reclaim is also racy, and unlock blindly deletes whichever lock currently exists. In-process lock waits ignore cancellation; a cancelled queued mutation can later edit settings.

Acceptance:
- Lock acquisition and stale recovery preserve one owner across processes; partial claims cannot be treated as stale.
- Unlock releases only its own claim.
- A cancelled queued service operation returns promptly and performs no edit, external command or misleading run-start.
- Focused Project/service tests cover contested claims, stale-owner recovery and cancelled waiting operations.

Dependencies: none. Part of PR #31 release reliability audit.
title: Project: preserve exclusive lock ownership and cancellation

body:
## Problem Statement

A person running self-host cannot see where every App stands in its setup workflow. The Dashboard shows one Status dot per App, and Needs action lists failures, but the path an App takes is invisible: rendered, images pulled, container started, each Setup step, each Link, the final check. During a long install, and after a crash or a partial failure, they cannot tell which Apps are done, which are mid-way, which are stuck and on what, or what a failed step needs. Pull, start and render only appear as transient footer text and are never remembered.

## Solution

A Workflow view on the Dashboard (key `w`), a step tracker across every App:
- Each App shows its ordered steps: render, pull, start, then its Setup steps, its Links, and check.
- Every step has a clear mark: done, skipped (already done), failed, running, or not run yet.
- The view updates live while an Action runs, and stays accurate later, because the Project remembers each App's render, pull and start stages alongside its Setup steps.
- A person can move through the steps, open a failed step to read its error and hint, retry an App's Setup, collapse or expand Apps, and filter Apps by name.

## User Stories

1. As a person, I want one view listing every App with all of its steps, so that I can see where each App is in its setup workflow.
2. As a person, I want the steps of an App in the order they happen (render, pull, start, Setup steps, Links, check), so that I can read the workflow top to bottom.
3. As a person, I want a distinct mark for done, skipped, failed, running and not run, so that I can scan states at a glance.
4. As a person, I want the view to update live while an install, update or Setup runs, so that I can watch progress without leaving it.
5. As a person, I want a step to show as running between its start and its end, so that I can see what self-host is doing right now.
6. As a person, I want pull steps to show image progress while they run, so that long downloads do not look frozen.
7. As a person, I want render, pull and start remembered per App after the Action ends and after restarting self-host, so that the workflow stays accurate across sessions and crashes.
8. As a person, I want a header counting Apps fully set up, failed steps and running steps, so that I know the overall state in one line.
9. As a person, I want to move between steps with ↑/↓ (and k/j), so that I can inspect any step.
10. As a person, I want enter on a failed step to expand its error and hint inline, so that I know what to do without leaving the view.
11. As a person, I want a failed Link shown under the App that declares it, with its target named, so that I know which App needs action (CONTEXT: a failing Link belongs to its consumer).
12. As a person, I want a Link waiting for its target shown as not run with the reason, so that I know it is pending, not broken.
13. As a person, I want `r` to retry Setup of the selected App, so that I can fix and rerun from where I am.
14. As a person, I want the retried App's steps to reset to running and update live, so that I see the retry happen.
15. As a person, I want space to collapse or expand an App, so that I can focus on the Apps that need attention.
16. As a person, I want Apps with a failed step expanded by default and fully set-up Apps collapsed, so that problems are visible first.
17. As a person, I want `/` to filter Apps by name or id, so that I can find one App among dozens.
18. As a person, I want esc to clear the filter, then return to the Dashboard, so that navigation is consistent with the other views.
19. As a person, I want the view to scroll (keys, pgup/pgdn, mouse wheel), so that it works with 90+ Apps.
20. As a person, I want every line to fit an 80-column terminal, so that it works over SSH from a phone.
21. As a person, I want Unmanaged apps listed as "added by hand, no Setup", so that I am not misled into expecting steps.
22. As a person, I want an App whose Setup never ran to show its known steps as not run, so that I can tell "not started" from "done".
23. As a person, I want the view reachable from the top bar and with `w`, and listed in help, so that I can discover it.
24. As a person, I want the footer to show the view's own keys, so that I do not have to remember them.
25. As a person, I want the step messages to use the same names as the CLI events, so that what I see matches what an agent reads.
26. As an agent, I want the remembered render/pull/start stages to appear in `self-host status --json` with the Setup steps, so that I can reason about the same workflow.
27. As a maintainer, I want the step tracker's logic in one module that turns Project status and live task events into the workflow, so that it is tested without a terminal.
28. As a maintainer, I want the view built on the shared view interface, so that it is tested in isolation like the other views.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Domain term.** Add "Workflow view" to CONTEXT.md: the step tracker showing, for every App, its steps from render to the last Link with each step's state. Amend ADR 0002 with the `w` key (it opens a view for a frequent need, within the view rule the amendment set).
- **Workflow module (new, deep, in-process).**
  - Input: the Project status (each App with its persisted step records in order) plus the events of running and finished tasks.
  - Output: one entry per App with ordered steps (id, label, state, message, error, hint, Link target when it is a Link, pull progress when running), plus counts: Apps fully set up, steps failed, steps running.
  - States: done, skipped, failed, running, not run.
  - Ordering: stage steps (render, pull, start) first, then Setup steps in recorded order, then Link steps, then check.
  - Merging rule: a live event for a step overrides its persisted record; a start event with no end means running; a newer run of an App resets that App's live steps.
  - The module performs no I/O; it is a pure function of its inputs.
- **Persisted stages.** The Project mutation module (which owns the order of every change) records per App the render, pull and start stages as step records, with the same ids the events use, so they survive the Action and restarts and appear in `status --json`. Existing Setup step records are unchanged.
- **Workflow view.** A view behind the existing view interface (Update/View/Keys/Title):
  - It reads the workflow module's output from the view context, and owns only its cursor, expanded set, filter and scroll.
  - Keys: ↑/↓ k/j select, enter expand a failed step, space collapse/expand an App, `/` filter, `r` retry Setup of the selected App (the existing Setup Action), pgup/pgdn scroll, esc back.
  - The top bar gains "Workflow"; the keybind audit gains `w`.
- **Live updates.** The view reads the task manager's events through the view context; no new polling beyond the existing refresh tick and task events.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests assert external behaviour through the highest seam: inputs and outputs of the workflow module; keys in and rendered text out of the view; JSON out of `self-host status --json`. Never assert internals (field layouts, private helpers).
- **Workflow module:** table-driven tests over Project status plus event sequences: ordering, every state, live-over-persisted merging, retry reset, Link attribution to its consumer, waiting Links, Unmanaged apps, counts. Prior art: the pure parsing tests of the pull progress parser and the legacy parity tests.
- **Workflow view:** isolated view tests over a small view context, as the existing per-view tests do: selection, expand, collapse, filter, retry emits the Setup Action for the selected App, scrolling, the 80x24 width check, plus a 120x30 golden. Prior art: the TUI view tests and goldens.
- **Persisted stages:** through the CLI with the fake Docker runner: after install, `status --json` lists render, pull and start for each App before its Setup steps; a failed pull records a failed pull step. Prior art: the CLI tests and the service mutation tests.

## Out of Scope

- A separate `self-host workflow` command (the stages reach agents through `status --json`).
- Editing or skipping individual steps, and per-step retry (retry is per App Setup).
- Historical runs and timelines beyond the latest state of each step.
- Showing steps of Apps outside the Project.

## Further Notes

- Builds on three recent changes: the Project mutation module (it owns the order, so it records stages), the deep Setup helpers (consistent "ready" step ids), and the view interface (one module per view).
- Use CONTEXT.md terms throughout: App, Unmanaged app, Setup, Link, Project, Action, Dashboard, Needs action.
title: Spec: Workflow view — a step tracker for every App's setup workflow

body:
# Spec: self-host, a single-binary TUI for self-hosting Apps

Vocabulary: `CONTEXT.md`. Decisions: `docs/adr/`. Design notes: `PLAN.md`.

## Problem Statement

Self-hosting a useful set of apps (a media server, a password manager,
notifications) means installing Docker, writing Compose files, choosing
images, fixing file ownership and time zones, then clicking through every
app's first-run wizard and wiring apps to each other by copying API keys
around. The previous `self-host` tool tried to automate this but is about
60k lines of TypeScript, needs a private repo, Bun, Node and an npm tarball
to install, and every app is a small bespoke program that an agent cannot
extend. When something breaks, nobody (human or agent) can tell quickly
what is running, what is reachable, what failed, or what to do next.

## Solution

`self-host` is one static binary installed with a single `curl | bash` line.
Running it with no arguments opens a full-screen terminal dashboard, in the
spirit of the Homarr developer CLI: a live table of the Project's Apps with
coloured health dots, a health pill summarising the doctor checks, an
updates badge, a sidebar with logs and Setup results, and many keybinds.
On a fresh host the same TUI walks the user through choosing a Recipe or
Apps, Host settings and an Admin login, then installs and runs headless
Setup with live progress.

Every action is also a plain subcommand with human or `--json` output, so
an agent can drive the whole lifecycle, read exactly what happened, and,
when automatic Setup cannot finish, take over with agent-browser using the
hint, URL and credential name the CLI gives it. `self-host skill` prints a
version-matched guide for agents.

## User Stories

### Install and first run

1. As a home-server owner, I want to install the tool with one `curl | bash` line, so that I do not need Node, Bun, npm or a source checkout.
2. As a home-server owner, I want the installer to verify the binary checksum, so that I know the download was not tampered with.
3. As a non-root user, I want the binary installed to `~/.local/bin`, so that I do not need sudo just to install it.
4. As a root user, I want the binary installed to `/usr/local/bin`, so that it is on every user's path.
5. As a user, I want `self-host --version` to print the version, so that I can report it when asking for help.
6. As a user without Docker, I want the tool to tell me Docker is missing and link to the official install docs (OrbStack on macOS), so that I know exactly what to do.
7. As a user whose Docker socket is not accessible, I want a clear message linking to the Docker post-install docs, so that I can fix permissions myself.
8. As a user with Docker but Compose v1 only, I want the tool to say Compose v2 is required, so that I do not get confusing errors later.
9. As a rootless-Docker or OrbStack user, I want the tool to use my active Docker context, so that it works without special flags.
10. As a user running under sudo, I want my Project created in my own home and files owned by me, so that nothing ends up owned by root.

### First-run wizard (TUI)

11. As a new user, I want the TUI to detect that no Project exists and start the setup wizard, so that I am guided from zero.
12. As a new user, I want to see the host checks (Docker, Compose, socket, disk space) as green/yellow/red dots before anything is installed, so that I trust the machine is ready.
13. As a new user, I want to choose Exposure (local network by default, or this machine only), so that I decide who can reach my Apps.
14. As a new user, I want detected Host settings (time zone, user/group IDs, umask, LAN IP) pre-filled and editable, so that Apps get correct file ownership and clocks.
15. As a new user, I want to enter my media and downloads folders with validation that they exist, so that media Apps are wired to the right place.
16. As a new user, I want to choose a Recipe (e.g. Media) or pick individual Apps with a filterable multi-select, so that I install exactly what I want.
17. As a new user, I want Homarr pre-selected but optional, so that I get a dashboard by default without being forced to.
18. As a new user, I want to type my own Admin login or let the tool generate one, so that I have one login for every App.
19. As a new user, I want App-specific inputs asked only for the Apps I selected, so that the wizard stays short.
20. As a new user, I want a review screen listing Apps, images, ports, Exposure, Host settings and Links that will be made, so that I approve exactly what will happen.
21. As a new user, I want to see live install progress per App and per Setup step, with a native terminal progress bar, so that I know it is not stuck.
22. As a new user, I want a recap at the end with every App's URL on my LAN IP and its Setup result, so that I can start using them immediately.

### Dashboard (TUI)

23. As a returning user, I want `self-host` to open a dashboard of my Project, so that I see everything at a glance.
24. As a user, I want each App row to show a coloured dot (green running and healthy, yellow starting or Setup incomplete, red stopped, unhealthy or failed), so that problems stand out.
25. As a user, I want each App row to show its URL, port, container state, health and Setup result, so that I do not need to run separate commands.
26. As a user, I want a health pill in the header that summarises the doctor checks as a green, yellow or red dot with a count, so that I know at a glance if the host is healthy.
27. As a user, I want a `⚠ N updates` badge in the header when newer images exist, so that I know when to update.
28. As a user, I want an Updates screen listing which Apps have newer images, so that I can update one or all.
29. As a user, I want a Doctor screen listing every check with its dot, details and fix hint, so that I can diagnose problems myself.
30. As a user, I want a Catalog screen to browse and add Apps and Recipes to my existing Project, so that I can grow my setup.
31. As a user, I want a Backups screen to create a Backup and restore one App or all, so that I can protect my configuration.
32. As a user, I want a sidebar showing the selected App's live container logs, so that I can see errors without leaving the TUI.
33. As a user, I want a sidebar tab showing the selected App's Setup steps and hints, so that I can see what was configured and what failed.
34. As a user, I want a sidebar tab showing the selected App's info (image, ports, folders, Links, credential names), so that I know how it is configured.
35. As a user, I want to filter the App table with `/`, so that I can find Apps quickly in a large Project.
36. As a user, I want keybinds to start/stop, restart, update, rerun Setup, remove, open in browser, and copy the URL or password, so that I can operate everything from the keyboard.
37. As a user, I want `?` to show a help overlay listing every keybind for the current screen, so that I can learn the tool.
38. As a user, I want a footer showing the most useful keybinds for the current context, so that I do not have to memorise them.
39. As a user, I want long actions (install, update, backup) to run as background tasks that I can watch in a tasks overlay and cancel, so that the dashboard stays responsive.
40. As a user, I want destructive actions (remove, purge, restore) to ask for confirmation in a dialog, so that I do not lose data by accident.
41. As a user, I want the dashboard to refresh automatically on an interval and when the terminal regains focus, so that what I see is current.
42. As a user, I want mouse clicks to select rows and switch tabs, so that I can use the TUI without memorising keys.
43. As a user, I want the TUI to adapt colours to light or dark terminals, so that it stays readable.
44. As a user, I want the TUI to lay out correctly on narrow terminals by hiding the sidebar and less important columns, so that it works over SSH from a phone.
45. As a user, I want the terminal window title to show the Project and health, so that I can see status from my terminal tabs.
46. As a user, I want Unmanaged apps shown in the table with a distinct label, so that I know the tool will not run Setup for them.

### Commands for agents and scripts

47. As an agent, I want `self-host install <app|recipe>… --set key=value --yes`, so that I can install without the TUI.
48. As an agent, I want a missing required input to fail immediately naming the key, so that I never hang on a prompt.
49. As an agent, I want `self-host apps list --json` and `apps info <id> --json` listing Apps, Recipes and their inputs, so that I can plan an install.
50. As an agent, I want `--json` to emit one JSON event per line (`run.start`, `step.start`, `step.ok`, `step.skip`, `step.fail`, `run.end`), so that I can parse progress reliably.
51. As an agent, I want each `step.fail` to include the App, step, error, App URL, credential name and a hint, so that I can finish the step with agent-browser.
52. As an agent, I want every `docker compose` command the tool runs logged verbatim, so that I can reproduce and debug it.
53. As an agent, I want secret values never printed in logs or events, so that transcripts stay safe.
54. As an agent, I want `self-host setup <app>` to rerun Setup and skip steps that are already done, so that I can retry after fixing something manually.
55. As an agent, I want `self-host status --json` to return Exposure, LAN IP, Host settings and every App's URL, state, health and Setup result, so that I can answer "why can't my TV reach Jellyfin".
56. As an agent, I want `self-host doctor --json` to check port bindings, firewalls and LAN reachability, so that I can diagnose network problems.
57. As an agent, I want `self-host credentials` to print the Admin login and per-App API keys on request, so that I can log in to an App to finish Setup.
58. As an agent, I want `self-host skill` to print a version-matched usage guide, so that I use the exact commands this binary supports.
59. As an agent, I want exit codes that distinguish success, partial Setup failure and hard errors, so that scripts can branch on them.
60. As an agent, I want a second mutating command to fail fast if another is running, so that two agents do not corrupt the Project.

### Apps, Recipes and Links

61. As a media user, I want the Media Recipe (Prowlarr, Radarr, Sonarr, qBittorrent, Jellyfin, Seerr, Homarr) installed and wired together headlessly, so that it works without clicking through wizards.
62. As a media user, I want Sonarr and Radarr connected to qBittorrent and Prowlarr automatically, so that searches and downloads work immediately.
63. As a media user, I want Jellyfin's admin account and libraries created from my media folders, so that I can start watching.
64. As a media user, I want Seerr connected to Jellyfin, Sonarr and Radarr, so that requests flow through.
65. As a Homarr user, I want every installed App added to Homarr with its integration, so that my dashboard is ready.
66. As a user, I want to install ntfy with its admin account created, so that I can receive notifications.
67. As a user, I want to install Vaultwarden with admin access configured, so that I can store passwords.
68. As a user adding Radarr later, I want only Radarr's Links (and Links pointing to it) to run, so that existing configuration is untouched.
69. As a user removing an App, I want Links pointing at it removed from other Apps, so that nothing references a dead App.
70. As a user, I want every App to use my time zone, user/group IDs and umask, so that files and schedules are correct.
71. As a user, I want port conflicts resolved by picking the next free port and showing it, so that installs never fail silently on a busy host.

### Lifecycle

72. As a user, I want `self-host start` and `stop` for one App or all, so that I can control what runs.
73. As a user, I want `self-host update [app…]` to pull newer images, recreate and re-check, so that I stay current.
74. As a user, I want `self-host self-update` to replace the binary after verifying its checksum, so that I get new Apps and fixes.
75. As a user, I want to be told in the TUI when a newer binary exists, so that I do not miss fixes.
76. As a user, I want `self-host remove <app>` to keep my data unless I pass `--purge`, so that removing is reversible.
77. As a user, I want `self-host config set KEY=value` to update Host settings and recreate only affected Apps, so that I can change my time zone or Exposure later.
78. As an agent, I want to add an Unmanaged app by writing its Compose file in the Project, then have start/stop/update/backup work on it, so that I can install things outside the catalog.

### Backup and restore

79. As a user, I want `self-host backup [app…] -o file` to write one compressed archive of App config and databases plus secrets, so that I can recover my setup.
80. As a user, I want each App stopped only while it is archived, so that database files are consistent and downtime is short.
81. As a user, I want media libraries excluded from Backups, so that archives stay small.
82. As a user, I want `--encrypt` to protect the archive with a passphrase, so that I can store it off-site safely.
83. As a user, I want a warning when a Backup is not encrypted, since it contains secrets, so that I make an informed choice.
84. As a user, I want `self-host restore file [app…]` to restore one App or everything, so that I can recover from a single broken App without touching the rest.
85. As an agent, I want Backups to be plain files with a manifest, so that I can schedule them and sync them with rclone or rsync myself.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Language and libraries.** Go (minimum version set by the newest Charm modules; Go auto-downloads the toolchain). TUI on `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (table, viewport, textinput, spinner, progress, help, key), `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (styles, tables, layer compositor for overlays and mouse hit-testing), `charm.land/huh/v2` for wizard forms. Commands with `spf13/cobra`. Backups with `klauspost/compress/zstd` and `filippo.io/age`. Everything else uses the standard library.
- **Bubble Tea v2 features used.** Declarative `tea.View` (AltScreen, WindowTitle, MouseMode, ReportFocus, native ProgressBar during installs), `KeyPressMsg` with bubbles `key` bindings and `help`, background-colour detection with `LightDark` palettes, focus messages to trigger refresh, `tea.Tick` polling, lipgloss compositor layers for help/tasks/confirm overlays.
- **Modules.**
  - **events**: one step logger with a human renderer and an NDJSON renderer; secret redaction at this boundary; the TUI subscribes to the same event stream.
  - **host**: Docker/Compose/socket detection, Host settings detection (TZ, PUID/PGID with sudo awareness, UMASK, LAN IP), free-port selection, doctor checks returning `{id, level: ok|warn|fail, detail, hint}`.
  - **project**: Project layout, include-list root Compose file, `.env`, `secrets.env` (0600), `state.json`, PID lock; discovers catalog Apps and Unmanaged apps from `apps/*/compose.yml`.
  - **compose**: the only place that runs `docker compose`; logs every command; parses `ps --format json`, `logs --follow`, `pull`.
  - **registry**: compares local image digests to the registry manifest digest for floating tags to detect updates (Docker Hub, GHCR, lscr).
  - **catalog**: registry of Apps and Recipes compiled into the binary.
  - **apps/<id>**: one package per App implementing the App contract (`ID`, `Info`, `Inputs`, `Compose`, `Setup`, `Check`, `Links`).
  - **helpers**: shared Setup toolkit: `Step(id, check, do, hint)` idempotent step runner, HTTP client with retries/auth, wait-until-healthy, container exec, secrets, XML/INI/YAML/JSON config edits, App URL resolution.
  - **backup**: tar + zstd archive with `manifest.json`, optional age passphrase encryption, per-App stop/archive/start, restore one or all.
  - **cli**: cobra commands mapping 1:1 to dashboard actions; exit codes 0 ok, 1 hard error, 2 Setup incomplete.
  - **tui**: model with screens (Apps, Catalog, Updates, Doctor, Backups), modes (normal, filter, confirm, help, tasks, wizard), sidebar tabs (logs, setup, info), background task manager, keymap, theme and badges.
  - **skill**: embedded agent guide printed by `self-host skill`.
- **Core service.** A single `Service` (Project + host + compose + registry + catalog + events) exposes the operations (status, doctor, install, setup, start, stop, update, remove, config set, backup, restore, credentials). Both cli and tui call it; neither talks to Docker directly.
- **Dependencies are injected** through one `Deps` value: process runner (for `docker`), HTTP client, filesystem root/home, environment lookup, clock, stdout/stderr. Real implementations in production; fakes in tests.
- **Compose layout.** Each App renders `apps/<id>/compose.yml` referencing `${TZ}`, `${PUID}`, `${PGID}`, `${UMASK}`, `${MEDIA_ROOT}`, `${DOWNLOADS_ROOT}`, and a bind address derived from Exposure. The root file only `include:`s app fragments. Config is bind-mounted under `apps/<id>/`; no named volumes.
- **Images.** linuxserver.io first, official images second, floating stable tags.
- **Setup contract.** Steps check first and skip when done; on failure they emit a hint and the run continues with independent Apps; Links run only after both ends finish Setup. No command marks a step done without its check passing.
- **Credentials.** One Admin login for every App; per-App API keys generated or read back from the App and stored in `secrets.env`; events reference credentials by name.
- **Exposure.** `lan` binds `0.0.0.0`, `local` binds `127.0.0.1`. Shown in recap, status and doctor.
- **Lock.** PID file; mutating commands fail if a live PID holds it; stale locks are replaced.
- **Distribution.** goreleaser builds linux amd64/arm64 and darwin arm64 with checksums; `install.sh` served from GitHub raw; `self-update` downloads and verifies the matching release asset.

## Testing Decisions

- Good tests exercise external behaviour through the highest seam and assert on what a user or agent sees: events emitted, files written in the Project, `docker` commands requested, HTTP calls made to an App, and what the TUI renders. They never assert on private struct fields when an observable result exists.
- **Seam 1, the Service with fake Deps.** All command behaviour (install, setup, status, doctor, update, remove, config, backup, restore, lock) is tested by calling the Service (or the cobra root with arguments) against a temp home, a scripted fake process runner standing in for `docker`, and `httptest` servers standing in for App APIs and registries.
- **Seam 2, the TUI model.** Screens, modes and keybinds are tested by feeding messages (window size, loaded snapshot, key presses, task updates) into the model and asserting on state and on rendered view text, following the Homarr developer CLI's `harness_test.go`. A few golden snapshots via teatest v2 lock the dashboard layout.
- **App Setup** is tested through Seam 1: each App gets a fake HTTP server modelling the subset of its API that Setup uses, and tests assert idempotency (second run skips every step) and the failure hint.
- **Real Docker e2e** per Recipe lives behind a build tag and runs nightly and on release in CI, not on every change.
- Prior art: `homarr-labs/homarr/tools/homarr-dev` (tui harness tests, docker parsing tests). The current repo has no Go tests.

## Out of Scope

- Installing Docker, public internet exposure (DNS, TLS, reverse proxy), VPN egress, scheduled or remote backups, monitoring stacks.
- Windows outside WSL; macOS Intel.
- Migrating Projects created by the previous TypeScript CLI.
- Browser automation inside the binary; agents use agent-browser themselves.
- Apps beyond the Media Recipe, ntfy and Vaultwarden.

## Further Notes

- The previous repo's `FINDINGS.md` and per-app notes document each media App's first-run quirks (forced auth on *arr apps, qBittorrent's temporary password, Homarr's onboarding); port that knowledge, not the code.
- `ajnart/self-host` already exists on GitHub with an npm placeholder; publishing `new-cli` there is a later, separate decision.
